articles.title: Draining peatlands is responsible for a few percent of our global warming
articles.summary:
Much of the focus for human-caused climate change is on fossil fuels, which are creating most of our problems. But land use change is also a large component of the story, accounting for about one-third of total historical CO2 emissions. Deforestation plays a major role here, but practices like draining wetlands also factor in. Exactly how much of our history of eliminating wetlands has contributed to warming is challenging to figure out. But thanks to new sources of data that measure emissions from today’s surviving wetlands, it’s possible to put a better number on it.

A new study led by Jevan Yu at MIT focuses on peatlands—environments like bogs and fens where organic matter accumulates into thick layers of material. Some 600 billion tons of carbon are held in these vast stores of peat, which is more than you can find in all the world’s living vegetation, the researchers note.

Because these areas are permanently inundated, any oxygen in the water is quickly used up, leaving the job of decaying all that organic matter to anaerobic bacteria that work much more slowly and don't digest everything. So instead of seeing organic carbon turning into the CO2 gas released by aerobic bacteria, in peatlands, a subset of it gradually turns into methane gas. Methane is an even more potent greenhouse gas than CO2 itself and ultimately gets oxidized into CO2. That means there’s a little trade-off from peatlands—most of the carbon they have is kept out of the atmosphere, but the carbon that does escape does so as methane.

The first-of-its-kind experiment worked beautifully as the solar-powered space probe slammed into asteroid Dimorphos, permanently altering its trajectory.

Using telescopes, astronomers measured changes in the orbit of Dimorphos around a larger asteroid companion named Didymos in the aftermath of NASA's Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission. The spacecraft released some 10 billion joules of energy as it impacted Dimorphos in September 2022 at more than 13,700 mph (6.14 kilometers per second), shortening the asteroid's 12-hour orbit around Didymos by about 33 minutes, 25 times the most conservative expectation.

But scientists could only learn so much from DART. The collision destroyed the spacecraft, as expected. DART recorded images as it took aim on Dimorphos, but only faraway telescopes and a small CubeSat that briefly detected the impact flash could see what happened next.

He didn’t ask because he needed to know the answer. He had actually solved this particular problem already. But he had never published the solution—which made it a perfect question to test how good AI was at physics.

LLMs have been trained on the whole Internet, so if a physics problem has been discussed online, it’s likely the model already knows about it and may have memorized the answer. So a fair test of AI capabilities needs to focus on problems that have never appeared online.

The model didn’t answer Raju’s problem correctly, but it did better than he expected—well, enough to get him thinking that the experiment should be repeated and formalized. With the help of a colleague, he set out to create a theoretical physics benchmark for AI.

The memos, which Reuters reviewed but Microsoft has not published, outline the response to the November 12 disruption. The company's post-incident report, dated November 20, attributed the downtime to an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July, which caused lock contention in the gateway processes. articles.title: How brewers can protect beers from smoke-tainted hops
articles.summary:
The 2020 Oregon wildfires burned over 1 million acres, destroyed thousands of structures, and killed 11 people. Smoke from the fires spread across the entire region; this "smoke taint" adversely affected not only local wine production, but also hops grown for beer brewing. Since the Pacific Northwest produces more than 95 percent of US hops and about 40 percent of the global supply, the potential economic impact is significant.

That's why Oregon State University (OSU) scientists have been studying how brewers could offset the negative impacts of smoke taint while still incorporating affected hops in their brews. Most recently, they found that it all depends on the quantity of tainted hops that are included and when hops are added during the brewing process, according to a new paper published in the Journal of the American Society of Brewing Chemists.

As previously reported, the chemistry of brewing beer is a very active area of research. For instance, in 2018, OSU chemist Thomas Shellhammer—who also co-authored this latest paper—identified the growing popularity of "dry hopping" (adding hops after fermentation, common for pale ales) among craft brewers as the likely culprit of the exploding beer bottle phenomenon.

articles.title: Kalshi makes “difficult decision” to halt Utah trading after losing court fights
articles.summary:
Kalshi made the “difficult decision” to pause operations in Utah after losing a court fight to block the state’s ongoing enforcement actions under Utah gambling laws, Kalshi spokesperson Jacki McGavick said Monday.

It seems Kalshi’s legal troubles in Utah have become too much for the prediction market platform to gamble on continued operations there. In Utah, several lawsuits are still playing out, and Kalshi also lost a bid to persuade a federal appeals court to block those cases until the appeal is resolved.

Kalshi also wasn’t saved by an emergency motion from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission—which argues that the CFTC has exclusive jurisdiction over prediction market trading. At this time, the federal district court has not granted that motion to block Utah’s enforcement actions, either.

articles.title: Homo erectus lived in the rainforest alongside Denisovans
articles.summary:
Homo erectus was walking around mainland Asia at least 60,000 years more recently than archaeologists thought. A handful of teeth from two caves in southern China's Guangxi Province just filled in a significant gap in the fossil record of a region that's vital to the story of how our genus, Homo, took over the world.

The chemical makeup of the teeth's enamel suggests that, over the course of their lives, these Homo erectus moved across surprisingly large distances and made their living in dense tropical rainforests—an environment we'd previously assumed that only our species had ever gained a real foothold in. And one of the teeth offers a strong clue that Homo erectus probably shared this vast landscape with the Denisovans.

A handful of teeth with a lot to say

Baxian and Naxian are a pair of limestone caves that lie 15 kilometers apart along a karst valley corridor in southern China. University of Copenhagen paleoanthropologist Frido Welker and his colleagues unearthed a total of nine hominin teeth from among the more than 18,000 bones and fragments from non-hominin animals found there. Macquarie University paleoanthropologist Kira Westaway and her colleagues analyzed proteins and chemical isotopes from the enamel of five of these teeth.

The abrupt reversal by Nvidia’s board was spurred by President Donald Trump, who applied pressure to the board over the weekend after watching what was once America’s most valuable company as well as the wider tech sector haemorrhage value last week.

articles.title: Amazon says hackers' AI agents found and exploited 0-day with little human input
articles.summary:
Amazon said AI agents recently found and exploited a zero-day vulnerability with no human oversight beyond a simple instruction to get root access on an East Asian university server.

The agents were running on Cairn, an open source AI penetration-testing framework. The hackers, who provided prompts in simplified Chinese and configured the model to the Chinese Standard Time zone, gave the agents a list of IP addresses and the goal: “obtain shell access.” In short order, the agents discovered a zero-day in an open source medical imaging AI application running on one of the target servers. The agents then exploited the vulnerability and gained full control of the system.

“These findings show that agentic offensive operations are already happening, and defenders should prepare for the speed and persistence these tools enable,” Amazon said.

articles.title: One terminal command gave my forgotten Android device a desk job
articles.summary:
My kitchen junk drawer used to hold takeout menus and coupons, but it has since become a storage spot for old tablets or phones. Like me, you probably have a few devices lying around that are perfectly functional but don't meet your daily driving needs. It's tucked out of view, living out its life in a drawer until being erased and donated after someone asks why you're holding onto outdated, unused devices. Thankfully, PhoneBox has a solution. You weren't hoarding old tech; you were waiting for the proper use.

The PhoneBox home screen displays useful stats and what's currently playing in your browser.
Credit:
Nick Indge

I had an old AllDoCube iPlay 50 mini Pro 8.4-inch tablet that seemed like the perfect candidate. I bought the tablet second-hand as a possible big-screen gaming and emulation tablet to use with a telescopic control deck, but I quickly found I vastly preferred just using a dedicated device. Since that realization, this decent little unit has lived its life in "the drawer."

Launch applications on your PC from the connected Android device.
Credit:
Nick Indge

Installation is a doddle

Getting PhoneBox up and running on my tablet and PC couldn't have been simpler. After making sure that the Android tablet was in developer mode, the process was as easy as plugging the tablet in to my PC via USB and executing a single copied command in my Linux terminal. The script downloaded the PhoneBox 0.9.29 software for my PC, verified the downloaded checksum against the release, and walked me through a few quick Y/N installation questions. The script offers to create a systemd user service, so the desktop agent launches after initial login, and even asks if you'd like it to install the PhoneBox APK to your connected Android device.

articles.title: Ukraine sinks Russian warship, strikes cargo ships from Mediterranean to Baltic
articles.summary:
Ukrainian explosive naval drones sank a Russian warship docked in the port city of Benghazi in Libya while also striking a Russian cargo ship that it was escorting. The incident demonstrates the expanding scope of Ukrainian military strikes on Russian ships from the coast of North Africa to the Gulf of Finland.

The Russian Navy’s missile corvette Merkury sank at port after being struck by at least two Ukrainian naval drones on November 22, according to The Associated Press. Ukraine’s Security Service described using seven naval drones launched from a mother ship to target the Merkury, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy shared video footage showing the drone boats approaching and exploding against both the burning Russian warship and a Russian dry cargo ship, MV Angara.

Zelenskyy noted that a Ka-27 combat helicopter onboard the Merkury was also destroyed. He described the cargo ship MV Angara as transporting weapons—Russia provides material support to the Libyan National Army that currently controls Benghazi and is battling the internationally recognized Libyan government based in Tripoli.

articles.title: States sue SpaceX to stop Grok from generating child sex images, revenge porn
articles.summary:
On Monday, Virginia and Oregon became the first states to sue SpaceX, alleging that Grok continues to sexualize, unchecked, real photos of mostly women and children.

SpaceX acquired xAI in February and now must handle the ongoing reckoning over the controversial rollout of Grok’s “spicy mode”—a model feature Musk hyped but was soon found to generate a flood of non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII) and child sex abuse images (CSAM).

Initial safeguards were so lax that Grok sometimes generated nude images without being asked. Although X Safety and xAI (now known as SpaceXSI) were silent at first, Musk’s companies eventually apologized and claimed that additional safeguards were implemented and policies redesigned to block harmful outputs. However, state attorneys general alleged that those statements were “misleading” and that SpaceXSI instead quietly “embraced” sexualized content to seize more AI market share, as Grok continues to generate NCII and CSAM today.

articles.title: Surveillance pricing uses our personal data to make us pay more
articles.summary:
“It costs what it costs” is a mindset I’ve found useful when encountering a sizable, but highly necessary or desired, expense. The sentiment encourages me to accept the price because that’s the accepted value of the gadget, app, or service that I really need or want.

But with surveillance pricing, that comfort is no longer a given. I could end up paying more for my TV because of where I am or more for a software subscription because of my age.

Surveillance pricing leverages data collected from our web history, smart devices, and apps with the goal of getting us to pay more. That obfuscates the value of products, challenges smart shopping and budgets, and makes it harder for people to get products and services at a fair price.

articles.title: Amazon fights Delivery Protection Act by putting stickers on its packages
articles.summary:
Amazon is placing a sticker on some of its delivery boxes to urge customers to oppose a New York City bill.

This weekend, some Amazon shoppers reported getting a delivery from Amazon with a sticker on it that reads: “NYC Council could add up to $5 per order. Act now to protect low prices.” The sticker reportedly includes a QR code that leads to a link for contacting NYC Councilmembers. The sticker encourages the package’s recipient to “Scan to tell your council member: no increases for New Yorkers.”

Amazon is looking to stoke opposition to Introduction 0518-2026 (518), also known as the Delivery Protection Act. The proposed law would require Amazon and other companies with last-mile delivery facilities in the city, such as FedEx, to directly employ third-party contractors Amazon uses for making deliveries.

articles.title: “Race realism” isn’t realistic—and it isn’t good science
articles.summary:
At this year’s World Economic Forum meeting in Davos, US President Donald Trump stated that people from Somalia have low IQs. “I always say these are low-IQ people,” he said in his speech. His son, Donald Trump Jr, made a similar statement about Haitian people in 2024 (Trump’s government has since ended the protected status of both Somali and Haitian migrants in the US).

These statements and their consequences are symptoms of a growing trend in Western politics: the re-emergence of racial views of human nature that have been largely in hiding for the past 70 years. Narratives about the innate intellectual inferiority of black or brown people compared with white people—which can still be found in academic journals today—are fuelling far-right propaganda in some of the world’s largest democracies. Such claims underpin misinformation strategies on social media and bolster political movements.

These narratives are sometimes euphemistically referred to as “race science” or more recently “race realism.” But, as we argue, they are not actually scientific. One member of this community, Nathan Cofnas, recently attracted public attention by accusing the late Jason Arday of plagiarism.

articles.title: Trump FCC declares California isn't allowed to enforce phone service rules
articles.summary:
The Federal Communications Commission ordered California to stop enforcing its Carrier of Last Resort (COLR) rules against AT&T, setting up another battle between the Trump administration and California over the state's right to enforce its own telecom laws and regulations.

AT&T's status as a Carrier of Last Resort in California requires it to offer telephone service to any potential customer in its territory. AT&T wants to stop offering basic phone service to new customers and discontinue service for 184,000 residential customers and 15,000 business customers on June 1, 2027.

The order released today granted AT&T's request to preempt state rules, following up on the FCC's previous approval of AT&T's petition to discontinue service. AT&T had tried to achieve the same result in court, but a federal judge rejected its request to override California's rules in July.

articles.title: Boatwright debuts strong as Gilas routs Syria in FIBA World Cup qualifiers
articles.summary:
MANILA, Philippines – Syria had no answer to the towering might and pinpoint shooting of Gilas Pilipinas as the favored Filipino squad rolled to a dominant 97-58 win to begin its campaign in the 2027 FIBA World Cup Asian qualifiers fifth window in Seremban, Malaysia on Friday, November 27.

Long-awaited naturalized player Bennie Boatwright made sure to live up to the hype in his national team debut, tallying a big double-double of 16 points and 13 rebounds, while frontcourt partner Kai Sotto led the new twin-tower duo with 18 points and 10 boards in just 17 minutes.

“We only had a few practices with Bennie Boatwright, and yet, he’s fitting into us like a glove,” said Gilas head coach Tim Cone. “He didn’t go out and force anything, and stayed in what we do. From a coaching standpoint, you like it, because it wasn’t guys stepping out of what they do, it was really within what we’ve asked them to do, and that was really nice.”

“I just think that the more Bennie is with us, the more he’ll get comfortable, and know where his teammates are, and know where they like to get the ball. We’ll know more about him as we go along. We just see him elevating his game more and more when he’s with us.”

While Boatwright and Sotto set the tone in the first half on the way to a 43-32 lead, star forward Kevin Quiambao seized the spotlight in the latter two frames, as he led an offensive onslaught from deep to finish with a game-high-tying 18 points, all off a 6-of-8 shooting spree from three.

Thanks to a 29-13 third quarter pullaway that featured a 6-of-7 team clip from downtown, Gilas fully negated its slow start to lead by as many as 40, 95-55, and rise to a 5-4 record in Group E. Syria, meanwhile, stayed at the bottom of the six-nation group with a 2-7 card.

“These games this late in the qualifying, this late window five of six windows, they are so absolutely crucial at this point. We brought by far our best team, I think,” Cone said.

“Our size kind of took over the game at some point. We just controlled the boards. I think we won it like, 60-30, or something like that. When you could do that, you can run up the score, and we were able to run up the score.”

After losing to undefeated Australia (9-0), earlier in the day, 84-67, Iran fell to a 5-4 slate ahead of its crucial clash on Sunday, November 29, against Gilas, which now enjoys a three-game winning streak after losing four straight.

A sweep of the Malaysia leg can put the Philippines on top of its Iranian rivals to boost its chances of World Cup qualification after a stretch of heartbreaking windows. Gilas ends its qualifying run at home in Cebu City in late February 2027.

The Scores

Gilas Pilipinas 97 – Sotto 18, Quiambao 18, Boatwright 16, Gomez de Liaño 11, Perez 10, Phillips 10, Ramos 5, Edu 4, Millora-Brown 4, Newsome 1, Thompson 0, Rosario 0.

Syria 58 – Atli 12, Harrison 10, Albalbisi 9, Idelbi 6, Hermes 6, Maran 6, Abdullah, Y. 5, Michelsson 4, Nounou 0, Abdullah, K. 0, Majak 0.

Quarters: 18-18, 43-32, 72-45, 97-58.

– Rappler.com

articles.title: DOH eyes faster upgrades for LGU-run hospitals in 2027
articles.summary:
MANILA, Philippines – The Department of Health plans to bring funds for the Health Facilities Enhancement Program (HFEP) down to the provincial level in 2027, to speed up infrastructure projects and the decongestion of DOH-run hospitals.

The Senate finance committee recommended an additional P5.4 billion for HFEP, pushing the proposed allocation to P15.58 billion, Senator JV Ejercito said during plenary deliberations on the DOH’s proposed 2027 budget on Friday, November 27. 

This comes after the House of Representatives approved only P10.09 billion for HFEP in its version of the general appropriations bill (HGAB), lower than the P14.54 billion allocated in the National Expenditure Program (NEP).

“Admittedly, ‘yong pagiging centralized ay talaga naging problema…for the whole fund to be utilized. Kaya nga po siguro one reason ‘yan [na] P4 billion natanggal sa HGAB,” said Ejercito, the Senate finance committee chairman and the DOH’s budget sponsor.

“But dito sa ating committee, binalik natin dahil may bagong programa ang DOH under Secretary [Edwin] Mercado, that is to download ito sa provincial hospitals and locally-run hospitals. So that they will [be improved, capacitated], para po ma-decongest ‘yong DOH-run hospitals,” he added. 

(Admittedly, HFEP being centralized became a problem for the whole fund to be utilized. Maybe that’s one reason why P4 billion was cut from the HGAB. But the Senate finance committee restored it because the DOH, under Secretary Edwin Mercado, has a new program, that is to download the funding to provincial hospitals and locally-run hospitals. So that they will be improved, capacitated, and to decongest the DOH-run hospitals).

With the limited funding, the DOH will also be prioritizing the completion of ongoing HFEP projects, particularly critical health facilities in remote and disadvantaged areas.

Ejercito said DOH-run hospitals, which are end-referral centers providing advanced or specialty care, currently have an average bed occupancy rate of 150%, especially with the implementation of zero balance billing (ZBB).

Since the ZBB rollout in July 2025, 4.2 million patients have benefited from the program in DOH-run hospitals, according to Ejercito. Recently, it was piloted in some hospitals run by local government units (LGUs).

In its version, the Senate realigned P19.8 billion from government assistance programs, including the Medical Assistance Program (MAP) and the Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations or AICS, to augment funding for the Philippine Health Insurance Corporation or PhilHealth.

Ejercito previously said the funds would go directly to hospitals to support the implementation of the ZBB program. This includes P7.6 billion for DOH hospitals, P2 billion for legacy hospitals, and P1 billion for LGU hospitals.

Aside from boosting the HFEP budget, the Senate also provided an additional P1.099 billion for health promotion, P1.599 billion for immunization programs, and P736 million for the Sulu Transition Program.

Phasing out MAP?

But if Senator Panfilo Lacson had his way, essential health programs would get even more funds while MAP would become a thing of the past.

MAP, previously called Medical Assistance to Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients or MAIFIP, has been tagged by watchdogs as “soft pork” and called a “politicized discretionary program.”

Acknowledging that the Senate might have to wrestle with the House regarding unfunding MAP, Lacson suggested introducing a special provision that would allow the remaining P16.2 billion for MAP in the proposed 2027 budget to be allocated to the chambers’ public assistance centers instead. He proposed having DOH personnel oversee the vetting process for claiming the medical aid.

Lacson said this was in a bid to eventually phase out the aid program.

“For next year, the DOH is planning to have a rules-based approach in granting medical assistance to qualified patients. They will, of course, study ‘yong inyong (your) proposal,” Ejercito replied. – Rappler.com

articles.title: The coral reef watchers saving our ocean
articles.summary:
BATANGAS, Philippines – In front of a house along the mangrove coast in Calatagan, Batangas, rafts and boats sat moored.

Jessie delos Reyes, 50, a slight-framed man who has lived in this house all his life, calls these rafts his floating classrooms; for more than half his life, he has dived in and out of the waters of the marine reserve just a few minutes away from his house. 

He is known as Kuya Jessie of the floating houses in Calatagan. His name is familiar to locals, tourists, students, and marine scientists who come here for fieldwork and retreat. 

The weather was fair that Tuesday morning in November. I joined Jessie on one of his dives to check the corals in Buntong Gasang, a coral monitoring site. The spot is a few minutes off the coast and not that deep. Buntong Gasang is adjacent to the Verde Island Passage, the famous waterway at the heart of the world’s Coral Triangle.

We used the floating classroom to go to Buntong Gasang. A motorized boat pulled the raft from the coast.

Three more divers made up Jessie’s team that morning — men who make a living teaching water safety skills, divers for nongovernmental organizations. That Tuesday, they were all volunteer divers for Calatagan Reef Patrollers or Carepas, which Jessie founded in 2004. 

On the floating classroom, they moved at ease with their scuba diving equipment. On the table was a green thermos filled to the brim with kapeng barako (barako coffee) and bread for a quick breakfast. 

SITE. A motorized boat pulls the floating classroom to transport volunteer divers to the coral monitoring site. Photo by Franz Lopez/Rappler

They used a laminated coral health chart — composed of several shades of coral colors — from Australia’s University of Queensland. Divers hold this chart against the corals to compare colors and grade them properly.

When it turns 1 — or the palest shade of each color — it means the coral has bleached. Once they’ve identified the right shade of the coral with the chart, they write the grade on their slates. They submit these reports to authorities and experts.

During the dive, Jessie delegated tasks to the team. The safety diver entered the water first to check the current. Jessie laid the transect and collected data, with another diver tailing him to assist. Then another diver took photos and videos.

About 30 minutes later, after surfacing from the water, Jessie said there was good news and bad news. The good news: some of the corals that were bleaching a month ago showed signs of recovery.

“But the bad news is most of them were recently killed,” Jessie said after the dive. “There’s algae already. They were not able to recover.”

After many years of monitoring the corals in Calatagan, Jessie has become an advocate for “citizen science,” where community members work alongside scientists to monitor changes in the marine environment.

“The marine biologists, marine scientists, come and go,” Jessie said. “The community, even when their eyes are closed, even when they’re asleep, they know what’s happening in the community.”

TRANSECT. Jessie delos Reyes holding a transect tape aboard the floating classroom while on the way to the coral monitoring site. Photo by Franz Lopez/Rappler

The promise of citizen science

Coral scientist Wilfredo Licuanan has always dreamed of municipal fisherfolk checking the health of corals and reefs all on their own. 

Licuanan, called Al by family and colleagues, is a De La Salle University professor who specializes in coral reefs. He established the SHORE Center, La Salle’s research center that pioneered a citizen science program on coral reef monitoring.  

Al, 63, grew up in Diliman, Quezon City — the third generation in their family to study at University of the Philippines (UP). He took up marine science as an undergraduate, only learning to swim the summer before his first semester, before later shifting to zoology.

At the former Marine Science Center (now Marine Science Institute) at UP, he was a research assistant to the inimitable Edgardo Gomez, the center’s founding director. He eventually left the center and joined the La Salle faculty in 1997. 

The next year, he started to manage the university’s Br. Alfred Shields FSC Marine Station in Lian, Batangas. The marine station lies in the western part of Lian, facing the Verde Island Passage and the West Philippine Sea. Its location is accessible to divers in the province, including volunteers from neighboring Calatagan.

Al said he has spent most of his time at the marine station as much as he could. Back then, it was still plain and bare, built like a bunkhouse along the coast in the remote part of town.

From 2014 to 2017, Al and his team at La Salle’s marine center surveyed reefs for a national assessment. The sheer scale of the work led them to develop further methods non-scientists could also use to assess coral communities and local reefs.

This eventually became the Alwan method. Alwan, a Tagalog word meaning “to ease,” evolved from the work of local and foreign researchers: an individual is trained to identify butterflyfish and target marine invertebrates and corals at a selected survey station.

By the end of the program, trainees are expected to know how to safely conduct a survey on their own, identify target species to determine reef health, and monitor bleaching triggered by climate change. 

TRAINER. Wilfredo Licuanan stands on the bow as water safety training starts in waters off the coast of Lian, Batangas. Photo by Iya Gozum/Rappler

Forty years ago, when Al started his coral studies, he did not deliberately set out to promote citizen science.

There are not enough scientists, and it would be impossible to regularly check on reef health without the help of people who are most frequently at sea: the fishermen, sea patrol, locals, lifeguards, and even recreational divers. 

“Those methods were actually an early form of citizen science in the sense that they were developed in Australia so that people who can dive but do not necessarily have the science training [can] do surveys in the Great Barrier Reef,” Al said.

On the field

A few weeks after my Calatagan visit with Jessie’s team, I joined Al and his SHORE Center staff in La Salle’s marine station in Lian. They had started training people from the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) on how to monitor reefs.

It was another Tuesday morning at sea. The water was cold, and I was swimming toward the reef crest in front of the marine station, following Al toward a jutting rock. He moved deftly in the familiar waters, while I tried to keep up. 

As we swam, the seafloor visible beneath me started to fade, and all I could see was blue. A few moments later, a blanket of dead staghorn corals appeared. I knew they were dead because of the fuzzy texture. Algae had grown and taken over. 

Above water, Al told me that amid the dead staghorn corals, there were new, living ones.

“I’ll point them to you,” he told me. We swam a bit more, and the live staghorn corals were hard to miss. Staghorn corals have branches, and these had white tips.

Al later told me that meant they were still growing. I asked him how there could be living ones among the dead. It’s the current, Al said. Corals may be spawning in another part of the reef, or in another reef altogether, and the coral eggs and sperm made it to the area due to the current.

SLATE. A diver takes note of target fish species on their slate. Photo from SHORE Center

A few minutes later, the BFAR staff who just finished water safety drills caught up with us at the reef. This was the first session of SHORE’s training for the BFAR. Among this session’s participants were the Carepas volunteer divers I visited in Calatagan weeks before.

Climate crisis and the decline of local reefs

Through the coral reef assessment from 2014 to 2017, Al and his team found a “marked decline” in the condition of local reefs in the past four decades (since the first assessment was conducted from 1976 to 1981). 

Many of their assessment stations were in Luzon, specifically in the Verde Island Passage. The marked decline in conditions led the team to report then that “the establishment of marine protected areas, and other interventions in the past 40 years have not caused an appreciable impact on overall reef condition in general, except in particular localities.”

“Mostly, it’s climate change,” Al said in an interview before their fieldwork in Lian.

“I keep saying it’s the most visible manifestation of climate change,” he added. “Because when the water is hot, that is not a localized event. It happens in large sections of the sea.”

LEARNING. A research assistant from SHORE (right) helps a BFAR staff with her fins before the water safety training starts. Photo by Iya Gozum/Rappler

The world is already on track to exceed the 1.5 degree Celsius limit that countries set to avoid the extreme impacts of climate change. At this point, drastic steps should already be taken to cut down greenhouse gas emissions.

Maintaining ocean health by protecting coral reefs, mangroves, and seagrasses can help cut down emissions. Australia and Turkey, co-presidents of this year’s largest climate summit, put the ocean at the heart of the conference, yet the talks broke down after a final draft deal failed to mention fossil fuels.

A way of life

Back in Calatagan, the coast opposite Jessie’s house was lined with mangroves.

“We planted those mangroves on September 2, 2002,” he told me after that morning’s coral monitoring session. “We have mangroves, we have seagrass, we have corals. The ecosystem here is complete.”

Jessie grew up in Calatagan. His parents fished for a living, and Jessie himself was a fisherman before he became part of the sea patrol, became a lifeguard, learned to dive, and eventually founded his volunteer divers’ group.

AFLOAT. The floating classrooms anchored in front of Jessie delos Reyes’ house in Calatagan, Batangas. Photo by Franz Lopez/Rappler

UNDERWATER. Jessie delos Reyes conducting coral assessment on November 3, 2026, in Calatagan, Batangas. Photo from Carepas

More than two decades ago, he attended a course that Al used to teach: marine biology for non-biologists. (“I taught it on the weekends,” Al told me in a separate interview. “Jessie was in the class.”)

Jessie has already seen it all: corals bleaching and recovering, the devastating impact of El Niño events in recent history, and typhoons that wreak havoc underwater.

His desire to protect the ocean is something he may have inherited from his parents, Jessie said
— from fisherfolk who were at sea every day and who saw what a healthy ocean looked like and what it could give them. – Rappler.com

Quotes translated to English for brevity.

This story was produced with the support of Informed Earth as part of the COP31 Ocean Virtual Reporting Fellowship.

articles.title: SM Nuvali brings a new flagship mall – and traffic – to Laguna
articles.summary:
LAGUNA, Philippines – SM has built quite a mall in the south – its biggest in Laguna, to be exact.

SM Nuvali, which officially opened its doors to the public on Friday, November 27, is a spectacle. At 190,525 square meters, it’s SM Prime’s 91st mall and the fifth in the province alone. 

But this flagship mall stands apart with its sprawling air-conditioned indoor garden and a glass-paned roof to let some sunlight stream in. On the floors above, restaurants and cafés overlook the patches of green, with playgrounds and a Paw Park.

“SM Nuvali is different because it brings together nature, sustainability, and thoughtfully curated retail experiences in one destination,” SM Supermalls president Steven Tan told Rappler. “At its heart is a garden within the mall, offering an outdoor-inspired environment that is air-conditioned and designed for comfort, while being LEED-certified.”

GARDEN. An indoor garden is the centerpiece of SM Nuvali. Photos by Leanne Jazul/Rappler

There’s a grand staircase, a community library called Book Nook with more than 10,000 books, and, on the top floor, a chapel.

Moviegoers can look forward to four regular cinemas, an IMAX auditorium with its own “IMAX Pods,” and two Director’s Club cinemas equipped with what SM calls the country’s first LED cinema screens.

MOVIE. SM Nuvali features the country’s first LED cinema screens. Photo by Leanne Jazul/Rappler.

And though it’s new, it’s far from empty. If you’re going for food, you’ll find all the usual suspects, which Tan told Rappler was “carefully curated” – Din Tai Fung, Wildflour, Hoshino Coffee, among others – but some are showing up in Laguna for the first time, like Michelin Bib Gourmand awardee Some Thai, Golden Yolk, George & Onnie’s, and The Matcha Tokyo.

Tucked in the Food Hall is SM’s Game Park, where you can squeeze in a round of billiards or arcade games between meals.

MEALS. SM Nuvali brings Makati’s Scratch smashburgers down south. Photo by Leanne Jazul/Rappler.

“Here, we can come together, enjoy a meal, and tell each other stories of our lives and our love,” Tan said at the mall’s opening gala on Thursday night, November 26. “We need community more than ever.”

Tan credited the Sy family “for their vision and passion to bring this development to the next level,” and then called SM Prime president Jeffrey Lim and Hans “Chico” Sy Jr. – son of Hans Sy and president of engineering, design, and development – to the stage.

CHEERS! (Left to right) Hans Sy Jr., Steven Tan, and Jeffrey Lim offer a toast during the opening of SM Nuvali. Photo by Leanne Jazul/Rappler.

In the crowd too was Chico’s sister Hanna Carinna Sy, senior assistant vice president for marketing and leasing. The third-generation Sys are now helping to design the malls, giving the newer ones a touch of youth. And of course there was Hans Sy, who looked on like the proud father that he was. (READ: SM Harrison Plaza opening by end-2027 with entire floor for Gen Z)

“I cannot tell you enough how excited we are to welcome people to a brand new home in the South. But that will be for tomorrow,” Tan said. “So tonight, we hold this moment to ourselves and celebrate!”

TYCOON. SM Prime executive committee chairman Hans Sy poses during SM Nuvali’s opening night gala. Photo by Leanne Jazul/Rappler.

But about that traffic

Tomorrow, of course, means cars, and probably lots of them.

Even before the mall officially opened, motorists and residents had already been complaining online about worsening traffic along the Santa Rosa-Tagaytay Road, particularly around the traffic lights in front of the mall.

SM Nuvali sits right at the Santa Rosa-Tagaytay exit of the Cavite-Laguna Expressway (CALAX), mixing mallgoers with motorists entering and leaving the expressway. With the height of Christmas shopping season approaching, congestion could worsen even for motorists who simply use the expressway to get home or travel to Tagaytay.

Asked about the traffic situation, Tan told Rappler in a message: “We recognize the importance of managing traffic, especially with the area’s continued growth. SM Nuvali is coordinating closely with the relevant local government units and traffic authorities to support traffic management measures, including proper vehicle ingress and egress, traffic flow management, and coordination during peak hours to help minimize congestion and ensure a smoother experience for motorists and visitors.”

When Rappler visited the mall on Thursday, traffic had partly backed up to near the CALAX exit. That was before the general public could even enter the mall. – Rappler.com

articles.title: X launches parental controls to help manage teen use
articles.summary:
MANILA, Philippines – Social media platform X on Thursday, November 26, announced it had introduced parental controls so that parents or guardians could better guide teens on their X usage and experiences on it.

The parental controls will not allow parents or guardians to read private messages, see searches or viewing history, post as their teen, or access a given teen account.

The social media platform, in its announcement, acknowledged that “while X is not designed for or promoted to children, and users must be at least 13 or older where required by law, we take extra care with the young people who are here.”

According to the X announcement, teen accounts “default to protected mode, sensitive media is restricted, and targeted advertising is blocked,” while parental controls give families further tools aside from these standard settings for teens.

The new parental control tools will let parents do the following:

see how much time their teen has spent on X over the past week

set limits on X usage

require approval for new followers (this also makes the account private)

limit For You recommendations and videos to accounts the teen already follows

control who can send direct messages to the account

filter specific words

turn off sensitive media content

see which accounts a teen has chatted with one-on-one (without seeing what they’ve written)

The X parental controls announcement is a long time coming. The feature addition is a first after about 20 years of operation, and comes after issues with X’s Grok AI chatbot being a vector for the generation of sexualized images or material featuring women and minors.

According to TechCrunch, while X is not generally aimed at teens, a 2024 study pointed to nearly a third of Gen Alpha kids as having an X account.

Michael O’Herlihy, head of safety at X, said in their press announcement that they aim to strike a balance between parental supervision and letting teens have some freedom to be themselves.

“Parents want practical tools, and teens deserve room to grow,” O’Herlihy said. “With Parental Controls on X, families can set the guardrails that fit their home, while teens keep ownership of their accounts and can see every change.”

A more thorough explanation of the parental control settings is available on this Help Center page. – Rappler.com

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Suan did not propose parliamentary gov’t if VP Sara isn’t impeached
articles.summary:
Claim: A video shows Cagayan de Oro 1st District Representative Lordan Suan saying that if Vice President Sara Duterte is not impeached, the law should be changed to shift the Philippines into a parliamentary form of government with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. as prime minister.

Rating: ALTERED

Why we fact-checked this: Multiple trending posts used a clip of Suan delivering a speech during the Cagayan de Oro Press Club’s 75th Anniversary Gala on November 23.

The video shows Suan supposedly saying, “Kung hindi man ma-impeach si Sara, gumawa na lang tayo ng batas para walang election sa 2028. (If [Vice President] Sara [Duterte] is not impeached, let’s just enact a law to cancel the 2028 elections.) Let’s transform the Philippines into a parliamentary form of government so that President Bongbong Marcos can become prime minister.”

A Facebook page called Defense Lawyers, one of the accounts that posted the video, wrote this as a caption: “Ano daw? BBM as Prime Minister?!!” (Say what? BBM as prime minister?)

The post garnered 11,700 reactions, 4,700 comments, and 1,700 shares as of writing.

Facebook user Amy Ugay also posted a vertical version of the video with a text overlay that says, “Oi Suan ikaw na lang kaya mag prime minister bakit si BBM pa tigilan mo ‘yan kahibangan mo.” 

(Hey Suan, why don’t you just become prime minister yourself instead of BBM? Stop this nonsense of yours.)

This post had 2,000 reactions, 742 comments, and 301 shares as of writing.

The facts: The audio used in the video is fake – Suan did not make any statement regarding Duterte, Marcos, or scrapping the elections in 2028.

A video shared by iFM CDO radio station showed Suan’s speech at the event, where he discussed the importance of the press amid widespread misinformation. He also mentioned House Bill No. 9397, or the proposed Right to Information Act, which seeks to institutionalize Filipinos’ right to access information on matters of public concern.

During his four-minute speech, Suan did not mention anything about the elections, Duterte’s impeachment, or proposing the country’s transition to a parliamentary form of government.

Suan’s office also categorically denied the claims, saying in a statement to Rappler on November 27 that the lawmaker remains an advocate of democracy and upholds Filipinos’ right to vote and choose their leaders.

His office added: “Walang puwang sa ating demokrasya ang sinadyang pagpapakalat ng kasinungalingan upang linlangin ang taumbayan.” 

(There is no place in our democracy for the deliberate spreading of lies to deceive the public.)

The Cagayan de Oro Press Club refuted the false claims in a Facebook statement published on November 26, clarifying that the congressman joined the event to show solidarity with local journalists and that he never uttered those statements.

“We call on vloggers and netizens to stop spreading unverified information that confuses the public and damages the reputation of our guests,” the statement read further.

Previous fact-checks: Rappler debunked multiple false claims about the 2028 elections:

FACT CHECK: ‘No 2028 election’ claim has no basis 

FACT CHECK: Marcos statement claiming to cancel 2028 election is taken out of context

FACT CHECK: ‘No 2028 election’ claim is ‘fake news,’ Malacañang says

FACT CHECK: Jonvic Remulla did not say Marcoses are ‘sure to be jailed’ after 2028

– Eirene Manatlao/Rappler.com 

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

articles.title: Pakistan Shaheens cruise into Asia Cup Rising Stars final with five-wicket win over Bangladesh ‘A’
articles.summary:
Pakistan Shaheens produced a composed five-wicket victory over Bangladesh ‘A’ in the second semi-final of the Asia Cup Rising Stars on Friday, chasing down a target of 233 with 28 balls to spare to book their place in Sunday’s final against Sri Lanka ‘A’.

The defending champions reached 233-5 in 45.2 overs after Bangladesh ‘A’ had posted 232-8 in their 50 overs. Hasan Nawaz, who made 62 and claimed two wickets, was named player of the match.

The chase was shaped by a measured third-wicket partnership between Hasan and Shahzaib Khan, who steadied the innings after Pakistan had lost both openers inside the first five overs. Shahzaib made 50 from 85 deliveries, while Hasan’s 91-ball 62 included three fours and three sixes.

Pakistan’s start had been unsettled by Bangladesh seamer Ripon Mondol, who removed the openers early and left the Shaheens needing to rebuild. Hasan countered with calculated aggression, including a six off Iqbal Hossain Emon that eased the early pressure, while Shahzaib concentrated on occupying the crease and rotating the strike.

The pair took the total to 128 before Hasan was trapped leg-before by Md Rubel in the 31st over. Shahzaib continued to anchor the innings, bringing up his half-century before falling for 50 in the 35th over to an excellent diving catch by substitute fielder Rizwan at midwicket off Rakibul Hasan.

With the innings requiring fresh impetus, captain Abdul Samad and Farhan Yousaf took charge. Samad struck 44 from 33 balls, adding momentum with forceful strokes through the leg side, while Farhan remained unbeaten on 46 from 39 deliveries.

Their partnership carried Pakistan through a testing middle phase, with the required rate kept within reach despite a couple of quiet overs and a near run-out involving Farhan.

Samad’s dismissal, with the target in sight, did little to derail the chase. Farhan kept his composure, declining unnecessary risks and ensuring the innings moved forward. Pakistan crossed the line in 45.2 overs, with Rohail Nazir alongside Farhan when the winning run was completed.

Earlier, Bangladesh ‘A’ had been lifted by a superb unbeaten 103 from Shahadat Hossain, whose innings rescued a side that had struggled for momentum in the opening half.

He faced 118 balls, hitting seven fours and three sixes, and shared a 95-run third-wicket partnership with Mahidul Islam Ankon to give Bangladesh a platform.

Pakistan’s new-ball bowlers made early inroads, with Ali Raza dismissing both openers inside the first five overs.

Bangladesh were reduced to a cautious start and reached 41-2 after 13 overs, before Shahadat and Ankon rebuilt through patience and selective attacking shots. Ankon contributed 30, helping Shahadat settle before the partnership was broken.

Shahadat then found another useful ally in SM Meherob, with the pair adding a half-century for the sixth wicket. Meherob made 28 from 36 balls, but Pakistan struck twice in the 41st over when Hasan dismissed Meherob and Rubel in quick succession.

Sufyan Moqim was central to Pakistan’s recovery, finishing with 3-29 from his 10 overs and preventing Bangladesh from accelerating during the middle overs. Hasan took 2-30, while Raza also claimed two wickets.

Shahadat’s late surge, including a six to bring up his hundred in the final over, pushed Bangladesh beyond 230, but the total proved insufficient against Pakistan’s steady response.

The Shaheens’ disciplined chase ensured that Shahadat’s determined century went in vain and kept their title defence on course.

articles.title: Govt increases wheat import ceiling to curb price increases
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: The government on Friday decided to increase the wheat import ceiling by 150 per cent to 2.5 million tonnes to check continuously rising prices of wheat and wheat flour in the market.

The decision was taken at a hurriedly called and virtually conducted meeting of the Economic Coordination Committee (ECC) of the Cabinet late at night, presided over by Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb.

The meeting was called in view of continuous increases in flour prices by 5-6pc on a weekly basis amid supply constraints.

The ECC “approved in principle the enhancement of the wheat import ceiling to up to 2.5 million metric tonnes (MMT) for Food Year 2026-27, to ensure adequate wheat availability, stabilise market prices and meet provincial requirements until the forthcoming harvesting season”, according to a statement issued after the meeting by the finance ministry.

The decision was taken after detailed consideration of a summary submitted by the Ministry of National Food Security and Research, seeking the enhancement of the previously approved wheat import ceiling from one million tonnes to 2.5 MMT. The decision will be placed before the federal cabinet for ratification.

The committee was informed that the provincial governments had initially assessed their wheat import requirements at 750,000 metric tonnes, which were then revised downward to 550,000 metric tonnes by the provinces themselves, according to the ministry.

“However, in view of the recent increase in wheat and flour prices and the need for enhanced releases from public stocks, the provinces have reassessed their requirements, raising the cumulative import demand to approximately 1.7 MMT,” the ministry statement said.

This includes 950,000 metric tonnes for Punjab, 450,000 metric tonnes for Sindh, subject to confirmation, and 300,000 metric tonnes for Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Balochistan’s requirements are to be met through available Pakistan Agricultural Storage and Services Corporation stocks.

The ECC agreed that enhancing the import ceiling to 2.5 MMT would provide enough flexibility to meet additional provincial requirements or shortfalls in available stocks, without requiring repeated approvals.

The actual quantities to be imported would be determined in accordance with confirmed provincial requirements and prevailing market conditions.

“The committee approved that the entire cost of imported wheat, including procurement, freight, insurance, transportation, port charges, taxes, duties and other associated expenses, would be borne by the respective provincial governments under the existing financial arrangements,” the ministry said, adding that the provinces would confirm their requirements in writing and ensure advance payments or appropriate banking arrangements in accordance with the agreed mechanism.

To facilitate the timely arrival and delivery of imported wheat, the ECC also approved priority berthing arrangements for wheat-carrying vessels at the relevant ports, in coordination with the maritime ministry and concerned port authorities, to minimise delays and additional costs, the statement said.

Regarding implementation of the arrangements, the committee agreed that while the Steering Committee headed by the Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar would continue to exercise overall oversight of the wheat import programme, the food security ministry would be responsible for its day-to-day monitoring, implementation and execution.

It also agreed that any operational or implementation issues requiring intervention would be brought to the attention of the Prime Minister’s Office on a real-time basis for prompt resolution.

While the ECC approved the enhanced wheat import quantities, the finance minister emphasised the importance of timely assessment of wheat requirements, effective management of available stocks and close coordination between the federal and provincial governments to maintain stability in wheat supplies and prices.

Aurangzeb said that wheat availability and price stability needed to be addressed together, with particular focus on ensuring adequate releases from public stocks and responding promptly to changing market conditions.

“He stressed that a coordinated and forward-looking approach was essential to safeguarding consumers from inflationary pressures while ensuring the efficient use of national resources,” the statement added.

The minister stressed the government’s commitment to maintaining sufficient wheat supplies and protecting consumers from unjustified price increases. He emphasised that the decision was intended to provide flexibility to meet emerging requirements, while sending a “clear message” to the market regarding the government’s resolve to maintain price stability, the statement said.

Aurangzeb stressed the need for a collective and coordinated response by all concerned authorities to “discourage speculative practices, prevent market manipulation and ensure that the benefits of adequate wheat availability reach consumers”, calling for close monitoring and timely implementation of the decisions taken by the ECC.

articles.title: Makkah pact nations review regional security, condemn Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
articles.summary:
A meeting of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement’s top decision-making body on Friday reviewed the regional security situation and condemned “persistent and heinous” Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

A meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) was held in the federal capital, where authorities announced a public holiday and imposed special movement restrictions in view of the high-level gathering. A local holiday was also announced in Rawalpindi.

The SPDC comprises the foreign and defence ministers and top military officials of the three countries. Friday’s meeting lasted approximately two-and-a-half hours.

Addressing the media after the meeting, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar thanked the participating officials.

He said that the SPDC comprised the foreign ministers, defence ministers, chiefs of defence forces and general staff of all three countries.

Dar said that he himself, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif and Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Asim Munir took part in the meeting.

He said that Saudi Arabia’s delegation comprised Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan and Chief of General Staff of the Saudi Armed Forces Gen Fayyadh bin Hamed Al-Ruwaili.

Meanwhile, Turkiye’s delegation consisted of Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, Defence Minister Yasar Guler and Chief of General Staff General Selcuk Bayraktaroglu.

“I would like to take this opportunity to thank our distinguished guests for their presence here in Pakistan,” he said.

“The SPDC meeting reviewed the evolving regional security situation and reaffirmed the determination of the three countries to continue working collectively towards peace, security and stability,” he said.

Dar said that the three countries reiterated their commitment to the pact, including collective defence, mutual solidarity and respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity.

“The three sides also reviewed progress towards implementing the decisions taken at the previous meeting of the Makkah Alliance for Defence and expressed satisfaction at the pace of progress towards the establishment and operationalisation of the alliance secretariat in Saudi Arabia,” Dar added.

He said the SPDC agreed to continue consultations to enhance cooperation and coordination between the member states in areas of mutual interest, and to support efforts towards de-escalation of regional tensions and encourage peaceful dispute resolution.

The states condemned the “persistent and heinous” attacks by Yemen’s Houthis on civilians and civilian infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, reaffirming their “collective resolve” to continue efforts in safeguarding Saudi Arabia’s security, sovereignty and territorial integrity in accordance with the “collective defence provisions” in the pact, Dar said.

He further stated that the three countries also pledged to strengthen cooperation in defence industries, joint technological development, training and capacity building “with a view to enhancing the collective capabilities and cohesion of their armed forces in order to address mutual security concerns and contribute to peace and security in the region.”

Dar added that the meeting not only symbolised the bond of “longstanding friendship and solidarity” among the states but also “represents Pakistan’s continued efforts towards regional and international peace and security”.

“The meeting also shows Pakistan’s growing and robust diplomatic footprint at the international level,” he concluded.

The Foreign Office (FO) also issued a joint declaration after the meeting.

It also said on X that during the meeting, Dar reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to the alliance and underscored the importance of solidarity and close coordination in addressing shared security challenges.

“He emphasised the purely defensive nature of the alliance and its role in promoting lasting regional peace, security and prosperity,” it said.

In a post on X, Asif hailed the alliance, saying it positioned Pakistan on the global stage as a “strong, responsible, and reliable partner”. He said the joint statement issued after the meeting represented a “historic and far-sighted step” for Pakistan.

“For the first time, three major Muslim nations — Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye — have formalised and institutionalised their commitment to collective defence, mutual solidarity, and respect for sovereignty,” Asif said, adding that the alliance sent a “clear message that the Muslim world is uniting to ensure its own security, rather than looking to others”.

“The establishment of a secretariat elevates this alliance beyond mere rhetoric, placing it on a practical and permanent footing,” Asif wrote.

He further stated that the joint declaration had prioritised de-escalation of tensions via diplomacy, adding that it aligned with Pakistan’s “long-standing” position on peace.

On the condemnation of Houthi attacks, Asif wrote that supporting the security of Saudi Arabia was a commitment to the stability of the entire region. The three countries’ pledge to cooperate on the defence industry, Asif said, presented Pakistan with access to “advanced technology, greater defence self-reliance, and economic benefits”.

“By leveraging Turkiye’s expertise in the defence sector alongside Saudi Arabia’s resources, Pakistan can elevate its own defence capabilities to new heights,” Asif said.

He reiterated that the pact was aimed at regional peace, stability and collective security.

“At a time when power politics is on the rise globally, this alliance of Muslim nations serves as a symbol of hope, trust, and a shared future. Long live the alliance between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye!”

Dar, Fidan agree to maintain ‘close coordination’ under pact

On the sidelines of the meeting, Dar met with his Turkish counterpart, where the two expressed satisfaction at the “growing momentum” in bilateral cooperation in trade, investment, defence and energy, the FO said in a post on X.

The FO added that the two leaders reaffirmed their commitment to each other on matters of mutual interest.

Dar and Fidan also agreed to “translate their strong political ties into tangible economic dividends and maintain close coordination under the Makkah Agreement for Joint Defence to promote dialogue and de-escalation”.

Fidan, for his part, thanked Pakistan for “warm hospitality” and the country’s “active diplomacy”.

PM Shehbaz expresses satisfaction at meeting outcome: PMO

Following the conclusion of the meeting, the delegations from Saudi Arabia and Turkiye called on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, during which the premier reiterated Pakistan’s commitment to the pact, a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said.

The prime minister also welcomed the “strong unity and determination” displayed by the three countries in defending each other’s security, sovereignty and territorial integrity in accordance with the provisions in the agreement.

PM Shehbaz expressed satisfaction at the outcome of the SPDC meeting, the PMO added.

The premier also expressed “unwavering solidarity with the brotherly Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, reassuring full support for its sovereignty, territorial integrity and security”.

PM Shehbaz also held a dinner reception in honour of the participants at the PM House, PMO said.

The alliance

The three countries signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement on Aug 7. The pact provides that an armed attack on any one member will be considered an attack on all, obliging the other two to extend assistance through available means, including military support.

The SPDC, which brings together the foreign and defence ministers and chiefs of defence staff of the three countries, is the alliance’s principal decision-making forum.

A permanent secretariat has been established in Riyadh to coordinate its work, with Pakistan’s retired Lt Gen Nauman Mahmood appointed as its first secretary general for a three-year term. A working committee comprising officials from member countries is also functioning.

Turkiye’s ratification of the agreement has completed the accession process for all three member states, but the alliance’s institutional and operational framework remains at what Asif described as a “nascent stage”.

“Initially, we need to have frequent meetings to steer what is being formulated, in a way that in the next couple of months we have everything in place so that we can move forward,” the defence minister said.

The alliance has yet to publicly define its doctrine, the composition of forces, command arrangements or procedures governing a collective military response.

An emergency SPDC meeting in Riyadh on Oct 5 had called for moving towards practical implementation of collective defence commitments, including arrangements for the rapid deployment of agreed forces and capabilities, subject to national laws.

Wider regional tensions

The alliance’s formation also comes against the backdrop of wider regional tensions involving Iran, the United States and Israel.

While the three members share an interest in strengthening regional deterrence, their differing strategic priorities make it important to define the alliance’s scope without allowing it to become an instrument for wider military confrontation.

Asif declined to comment on how the alliance would respond to a direct Iranian attack on Saudi Arabia, but identified Israel as a possible threat to other countries in the region.

“The possibility of some conflict, or aggression from the Israeli side exists, so we need to close our ranks, the countries of this region,” he said.

Managing relations with Iran will be particularly important for Pakistan, which has sought to preserve diplomatic engagement with Tehran while deepening defence cooperation with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.

A meeting in Tehran involving representatives of the three countries and Iranian officials, held on Pakistan’s initiative, reflected efforts to keep channels of communication open between the two sides.

Pakistan brokered a June accord that led to a brief halt in fighting between the US and Iran and laid out a roadmap for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and negotiations on Tehran’s nuclear programme.

However, the truce collapsed, with Washington and Tehran accusing each other of violating the agreement, prompting months of shuttle diplomacy led principally by Qatar and Pakistan.

Asif said Pakistan had played “a very, very constructive role” between Washington and Tehran, but the outcome of ongoing mediation was “still fragile” and peace was “not yet embedded in a way people were expecting”.

Recent Pakistani military deployments, including JF-17 aircraft, drones and air defence systems such as the HQ-9, were made under bilateral cooperation predating the alliance, a security source said, adding that these existing arrangements would now become part of the trilateral framework.

Meanwhile, Turkiye has stressed the defensive character of the agreement and remained cautious about involvement in combat operations in Yemen.

articles.title: President Zardari, PML-Q chief Shujaat discuss country's political situation
articles.summary:
President Asif Ali Zardari on Friday discussed the country’s political situation in a meeting with former prime minister and Pakistan Muslim League-Quaid (PML-Q) chief Chaudhry Shujaat Hussain.

In a statement, the Presidency said that President Zardari held the meeting with Shujaat at the latter’s residence in Lahore, where Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi was also present.

“National affairs and the political situation were discussed during the meeting,” the statement said.

The president wished the PML-Q leader a speedy recovery, it added.

According to the statement, Punjab Governor Sardar Saleem Haider, federal minister Chaudhry Salik Hussain, provincial minister Chaudhry Shafiq Hussain, former prime minister Raja Pervez Ashraf, Senator Saleem Mandviwalla and Dr Asim also attended the meeting.

The meeting comes in the wake of an ongoing debate over the creation of new provinces and the holding of a referendum, with President Zardari’s PPP opposing the move.

The debate was sparked by Naqvi’s July remarks, wherein he called for the formation of new administrative units in the country, saying the current “system” of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”.

Earlier this week, Naqvi also held a meeting with Shujaat, where the debate over the creation of new provinces and devolution of powers was discussed.

During the meeting, Shujaat said the question of creating new provinces was directly linked to public convenience, good governance, administrative efficiency and the country’s future.

In the meeting, Naqvi and Shujaat discussed the overall political situation, measures to maintain law and order, and the need to transfer power to the grassroots level.

Later that day, Naqvi met Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, with whom he discussed the prevailing situation.

articles.title: Petrol price reduced by Re1 per litre, diesel price kept unchanged
articles.summary:
The government on Friday reduced the price of petrol by Re1 per litre while keeping the price of diesel unchanged, according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs312 per litre and high-speed diesel (HSD) at Rs346 per litre until Nov 30 (Monday).

The prices of HSD and petrol have gone below the July 18 rate of Rs354.35 and Rs316.15 per litre, respectively, as a result of price reductions made to both on Wednesday.

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Under an arrangement announced on Nov 2, for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

On Sept 17, the government rolled out the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme across the country to ease the public’s burden amid rising fuel prices due to the Middle East situation.

The subsidy scheme applies to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc.

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.

Since July 17, the government has been revising fuel prices on a near-daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the conflict. The federal government had also announced targeted relief measures in April to provide subsidised fuel.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

articles.title: 3 convicted of taking woman from UK to Pakistan, forcing her into marriage: police
articles.summary:
Police in the United Kingdom said on Friday that three people had been convicted of taking a young woman from the country to Pakistan and forcing her into marriage.

A statement issued by West Midlands Police noted that the woman was “particularly vulnerable” to exploitation as she did not have the capacity to consent to marriage.

“This conviction is understood to be the first in the UK which centres around a victim not being deemed to have capacity to consent to marriage,” police said.

“Mohammad Bashir, Khatoon Bi and Mobeen Akhtar, all from Birmingham, took advantage of a vulnerable woman in autumn 2024,” the statement said, adding that the police were alerted to the exploitation in early November of that year and immediate inquiries were carried out by their public protection unit.

According to police, the investigators learned that the involved parties were returning to the UK “within days”. Officers detained the three on Nov 7, 2024 at Birmingham Airport on suspicion of forced marriage.

“We also safeguarded the woman and, after speaking to her, we established she was unaware how she had been exploited,” the police said.

Deputy Senior Investigating Officer (DSIO) Mindy Mahil, one of the officers leading the investigation, said, “These three took advantage of a young woman, who was extremely vulnerable, and took her from Birmingham to Pakistan for marriage.

“It became clear to us immediately that the woman was being exploited, and that she did not have capacity to consent to a marriage.”

According to Mahil, the welfare of the woman was the priority throughout the sensitive inquiry.

“Forcing someone into marriage without their consent is abuse and control, and we will always seek to pursue offenders and support victims,” the DSIO said.

Following the trial at Birmingham Crown Court, Bashir, aged 55, Bi, 55, and Aktar, 38, were convicted of the offence and will be sentenced at a later date, the statement said.

articles.title: Man buried under rubble rescued alive 2 days after building collapse in Karachi’s Baloch Colony
articles.summary:
KARACHI: A man buried under the rubble from the collapse of an under-construction six-storey building near Karachi’s Baloch Colony was rescued alive on Friday, two days after the incident occurred.

On Wednesday, three people were killed and 14 others injured when the under-construction building — reportedly being constructed illegally on a residential plot — collapsed. Another body was recovered on Thursday, taking the death toll to four. On Friday, four more bodies were recovered, taking the toll to eight.

Rescue 1122 said on Friday that 28-year-old Muhammad Adil was rescued alive from the rubble. It said that the search operation for any other individuals feared trapped was underway.

Its spokesperson, Hassaanul Haseeb Khan, termed the rescue a “breakthrough”. He added that rescue operations were ongoing to search for other survivors from the debris.

He said the rescued man told them that two other persons who might be alive were in touch with him. However, Khan said the rescuers conducted a search in the identified area but could not locate them.

Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah expressed gratitude that the man trapped under the rubble survived for 54 hours, describing it as a “miracle”, according to a statement issued from his office.

According to the statement, the chief minister directed rescue agencies and the Karachi commissioner to accelerate the ongoing rescue operation and deploy all available resources.

Murad also praised rescue workers for their tireless efforts and directed officials to ensure the survivor receives the best possible medical treatment.

The statement added that CM Murad had ordered a comprehensive investigation into the building collapse, warning that action would be taken against those found responsible for negligence.

Death toll rises to 8

In a separate statement, Rescue 1122 said the total number of bodies recovered from the rubble had reached eight.

The service’s spokesperson told Dawn that 11 people were still missing according to reports submitted by their relatives at the information desk set up at the site of the collapsed building.

He said it may not be advisable for the workers to provide a timeline for finishing the rescue and debris removal operation at this stage.

Khan said that heavy machinery was also being used to remove debris, but that whenever a human body was spotted in the debris, the team stopped the machine operations and initiated manual work with extra care to recover the body.

He admitted that this pace of the rescue operation may be causing concern for the relatives of the missing persons, who were protesting the slowness of the operation.

Newly-appointed East Deputy Commissioner Kashif Nabi Khuhro, speaking to the media, denied that the pace of the rescue operation was slow. However, he pointed out that the collapsed building was situated in congested and narrow streets, where it was relatively difficult to move heavy machinery.

Sindh Local Government Secretary Waseem Shamshad, who also served as director general of the Sindh Building Control Authority (SBCA), was removed from both posts on Thursday on the directives of CM Murad following the incident.

The CM ordered sweeping action over the incident while chairing a high-level meeting, further issuing directives for the removal of East Deputy Commissioner Nasrullah Abbasi, as well as Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) East Zubair Sheikh over “negligence”, a statement issued by the CM Office said.

In addition to the removal of the three officials, CM Murad further issued directives for the suspension of 16 SBCA officials and the initiation of an inquiry against them.

He directed the police to “immediately” arrest the building’s owner, Salman Tahir, and the builder, Zeeshan.

Moreover, he instructed that the building’s architect and structural engineer be included in the incident’s investigation to determine whether the construction complied with approved plans, building regulations and safety standards.

14 ‘illegal’ buildings in KAEHS to be demolished

The KDA’s Additional Deputy DG Farhan Kaiser visited the site on Thursday and told the media that their first priority was to remove the debris. He said that under the directions of the Sindh CM and LG minister, “illegal buildings” were being sealed across the metropolis.

He said that so far, 14 buildings had been sealed in the KAEHS after the building collapse and would be demolished in a second phase of the operation.

Kaiser added that it was the responsibility of the residents to report illegal buildings in their respective areas, and vowed to take action against the builders and owners of these buildings.

Members of the Chief Minister Inspection Team (CMIT), Bilal Memon and Anwar Shar, visited the scene and collected samples of the material used in the construction of the building for investigation purposes.

Rehabilitation secretary Rafiq Mustafa Shaikh, SBCA DG Abid Saleem, Rescue 1122 DG Brig. (retd) Wajid Sibghatullah Mahar and Rescue 1122 COO Dr Abid Jalaluddin Shaikh also visited the site and supervised the rescue operation.

FIR registered

A first information report (FIR) of the incident was registered at the Tipu Sultan police station on Wednesday, on the complaint of an official of the Sindh Local Government Department.

The FIR, seen by Dawn, invoked Sections 302 (intentional murder), 119 (public servant concealing design to commit offence), 427 (mischief causing damage), 337-H(1) (hurt caused by rash or negligent act), 109 (abetment) and 34 (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention) of the Pakistan Penal Code.

The building’s four owners — including Salman Tahir whose arrest the Sindh CM has ordered — its builder, architect, structural engineer and its contractors have been nominated in the FIR.

According to the FIR, the complainant alleged that poor-quality material was being used in the construction of the building. He claimed that the suspects, in collusion with the officials of various government departments, had been involved in constructing additional structures and not complying with the building’s approved plan.

This was why the building collapsed around 1pm, the complainant alleged.

Police have arrested four of the suspects, including one of the owners, Saad Tahir, and three contractors, who were produced before the judicial magistrate (south) today.

The judge granted police a five-day physical remand of the suspects.

articles.title: SBP issues Rs200 commemorative coin to mark Mata Sahib Hasi Devi’s 200th birth anniversary
articles.summary:
The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) has issued a Rs200 commemorative coin to mark the 200th birth anniversary of Pujya Mata Sahib Hasi Devi, the bank said in a statement on Friday.

Mata Sahib Hasi Devi was the fifth head of the historic Shadani Darbar located in the Hayat Pitafi area of Sukkur division’s Ghotki district.
