According to the statement, the coin has been issued through the exchange counters of all field offices of the SBP Banking Services Corporation from Friday.

The coin is made of cupro-nickel, comprising 75 per cent copper and 25pc nickel. It measures 30 millimetres in diameter and weighs 13.5 grammes, the statement said.

It added that the face of the coin features a waxing crescent moon and five-pointed star in the centre, facing northwest in a rising position. Along the periphery on top of the crescent and star is inscribed “Islami Jamhuria Pakistan” (Islamic Republic of Pakistan) in Urdu.

Below the crescent, at the top of the two wheat springs with their arms curved upwards, is the year of issuance 2026. The coin’s value and “rupia” in Urdu script are inscribed on the right and left sides of the crescent and star, respectively.

Meanwhile, the back features a picture of Puj Shandani Darbar in the centre. The inscription “Pujya Mata Sahib Hasi Devi” appears at the top along the periphery, while the wording “200th birth anniversary” is written along the lower periphery.

The years 1826 and 2026 are written on the left and right sides of the picture, respectively, marking the 200th birth anniversary, the statement said.

Last month, Pakistan Post also issued two special commemorative postage stamps and a souvenir sheet for the 200th birth anniversary of Mata Sahib Hasi Devi to promote interfaith harmony and Sufi traditions in the region.

articles.title: Indian police say they rescued 164 foreigners trafficked for cyber fraud
articles.summary:
Indian police said they had rescued 164 foreign nationals allegedly trafficked into the country and forced to commit online fraud, in a rare case involving victims from overseas.

Fraud compounds, where international scammers lure internet users into fake romantic relationships, cryptocurrency investments and betting platforms, are common in Southeast Asia.

While similar crimes are also widespread in India, it is much less common for the ringleaders to traffic foreigners into the country to perpetrate them.

A police crackdown on an international cybercrime network in a suburb of the capital New Delhi resulted in the rescue of 92 Indonesian nationals and 72 Malaysians, the force said.

The individuals were trafficked into India “on various pretexts, including promises of employment and lucrative opportunities”, it said in a statement late on Thursday.

“After their arrival, the foreign nationals were allegedly confined and compelled to participate in cyber fraud activities.”

Investigators have arrested a Malaysian national, whose role is “being investigated”, and identified two Indian handlers, police said.

A United Nations report estimated this year that at least 300,000 people have been trafficked into scam compounds across Southeast Asia.

New Delhi repatriated more than 2,400 Indians from cyberscam centres in neighbouring Myanmar in the past year, according to the foreign ministry.

articles.title: Roads blocked, traffic congested in Karachi for 2nd consecutive day
articles.summary:
Karachi saw blocked roads and congested traffic for a second consecutive day on Friday as road closure alerts caused traffic to be diverted due to a protest around the Karachi Press Club (KPC).

The city’s traffic police earlier announced diversions around KPC ahead of an expected protest, advising commuters to use alternative routes to avoid inconvenience.

According to a press release, the traffic heading from MR Kiyani Chowk towards Saddar and Zainab Market would be diverted left from Coast Guards Mess towards the Sindh High Court (SHC) and Passport Office.

It added that Sharea Faisal could be closed temporarily at Avari traffic signal.

Traffic travelling from Sharea Faisal towards the airport would be diverted right from Avari traffic signal onto Fatima Jinnah Road, towards Cantt, School Road, CSD and Kala Pul, the release said.

According to updates issued by the traffic police, the road from Coast Guard towards Zainab Market and Sarwar Shaheed Road was closed to traffic at around 3:20pm in view of security.

Traffic from Coast Guard was being sent towards the Chowrangi Passport Office, while traffic coming from there was being directed towards Paradise Chowk, the traffic police said.

The road was later re-opened to traffic as of an alert at 6:05pm.

Drigh Road towards Karsaz and Sharea Faisal was closed to traffic at around 4pm, with traffic being rerouted from Drigh Road via the Rashid Minhas Flyover towards Millennium.

The road was opened about half-an-hour later, but an alert was issued for heavy traffic pressure as the traffic was only running in one lane, slowing the movement of vehicles.

At 5:22pm, the traffic police issued an update that the flow of traffic had been restored, with all lanes opened for traffic. It noted that peak hours were still ongoing but that traffic was being kept moving.

Another road closure alert was issued for the road from Avari Towers towards Mehran Hotel and Sharea Faisal at 5:10pm. Traffic is being sent via Avari Towers towards Fatima Jinnah Road, police said.

Motorists were earlier advised to avoid roads around the KPC and follow the traffic police’s instructions. The public was also urged to cooperate with law enforcement agencies and traffic police.

Commuters requiring assistance could contact the Traffic Police Rahnuma helpline at 1915, where representatives would be available round the clock to provide guidance.

The latest traffic updates are also available through Karachi Traffic Police’s social media platforms, the statement added.

articles.title: Short-term inflation clocks in at 9.49pc driven by wheat flour prices
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: Short-term inflation was recorded at 9.49 per cent year-on-year in the week ending on Nov 26, driven largely by wheat flour prices, according to official data released by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) on Friday.

The index comprises 51 items, with prices collected from 50 markets in 17 cities, and is calculated weekly to track changes in the prices of essential commodities and services.

The data showed that the prices of 20 commodities increased, while those of nine items declined. Meanwhile, the prices of 22 items remained unchanged from the previous week.

Short-term inflation has entered single digits after several weeks owing to a decline in petroleum products prices. It had remained in the double digits for several consecutive weeks, largely due to persistently elevated petrol and diesel prices.

During the 25 days leading up to Nov 27, petrol prices fell from Rs396.06 to Rs313 per litre, while diesel prices declined from Rs398.80 to Rs346 per litre. This represented reductions of about Rs83 and Rs52 per litre, respectively.

The impact of this decline was visible in the week-on-week review. The Sensitive Price Index (SPI) declined by 0.11pc week-on-week, reflecting declining oil prices. This is the third consecutive week that SPI recorded a marginal decline on a week-on-week basis.

However, the provincial governments have yet to take urgent measures to reduce passenger and freight fares in line with the decline in petrol and diesel prices. Due to these high fares, the prices of perishable products are also higher.

Meanwhile, the items that recorded the highest price increases over the previous week included wheat flour (5.72pc), electricity for Q1 (5.43pc), eggs (4.36pc), chicken (4.14pc), garlic (1.54pc), rice basmati broken (0.79pc), potatoes (0.78pc), pulse gram (0.57pc), match box (0.47pc), bread plain (0.44pc), firewood (0.24pc) and washing soap (0.19pc).

Items that recorded week-on-week price declines included tomatoes (23.92pc), onions (21.27pc), LPG (7.78pc), petrol (2.48pc), diesel (1.99pc), pulse masoor (0.68pc), sugar (0.24pc) and bananas & pulse mash (0.12pc) each.

On an annual basis, the items that recorded the highest price increases included LPG (67.49pc), wheat flour (53.53pc), chicken (30.10pc), electricity for Q1 (29.33pc), diesel (22.36pc), petrol (18.34pc), chillies powder (15.55pc), mutton (14.59pc), bread plain (12.85pc), beef (11.09pc), pulse gram (9.62pc) and milk fresh (8.96pc).

In contrast, sugar prices fell by 26.56pc, potatoes (23.04pc), tomatoes (15.91pc), eggs (11.78pc), salt powder (8.78pc), pulse moong (7.57pc), pulse masoor (7.29pc) and gur (5.71pc).

Last week, short-term inflation was recorded at 10.41pc year-on-year, driven largely by wheat flour prices. Prior to that, short-term inflation rose to 11.21pc year-on-year, driven largely by perishable food products.

articles.title: Airline Norse Atlantic's Norwegian operating unit declares bankruptcy
articles.summary:
Airline Norse Atlantic’s Norwegian operating unit has declared bankruptcy, the long-haul budget carrier said on Friday, succumbing to soaring fuel costs wrought by the war on Iran.

Norse Atlantic ASA, which is listed on the Oslo Euronext Expand bourse, and other group companies are not part of the filing and are still attempting to stay in business, the company said in a statement.

Norse Atlantic, which launched in 2022, on Wednesday warned that its financial situation was “critical”, and the following day said it had suspended all flights and that the board could file for bankruptcy unless it urgently secured funding.

Earlier on Friday, Norse said its lessors had terminated their leasing contracts for all 12 aircraft in the carrier’s fleet, demanding that the planes be handed back, a claim contested by the company.

“The Board of Norse Atlantic Airways AS has made the difficult decision to file for bankruptcy despite extensive efforts from the company and the group to find a solution,” Norse CEO Eivind Roald said in a statement.

“The board, management and advisers of the listed entity Norse Atlantic ASA and the UK subsidiary are working to find a solution for the remaining part of the business to continue operations,” Roald said.

The global aviation industry is suffering its worst crisis since the Covid-19 pandemic as the US-Iran conflict, which began at the end of February, disrupts operations, drives up fuel prices, and sends airlines’ costs skyrocketing.

Pakistan International Airlines (PIA), a wet-lease partner of the airline, said earlier that it would shift its UK operations to its own Boeing 777 fleet from Nov 26 after Norse Atlantic abruptly suspended operations, forcing the cancellation of two flights from London and Manchester.

Norse in 2021 signed long-term leases for nine Boeing 787 Dreamliner aircraft from Ireland-based AerCap Holdings and six Dreamliners from Singapore-based BOC Aviation Ltd. It later returned three of the planes to AerCap.

In October, PIA signed an ACMI (aircraft, crew, maintenance, and insurance) lease agreement with Norse Atlantic Airways to acquire two state-of-the-art Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners, one of which arrived in Islamabad on Nov 1.

A PIA spokesperson at the time said the addition of the Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner would mark the start of the expansion of the airline’s fleet as it aimed to meet rising demand.

articles.title: ADB approves $468m in loans to boost water, agriculture management in KP and Punjab
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) on Friday approved two loans totalling $468 million to improve water and agriculture management in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Punjab.

According to the bank, the financing will strengthen community resilience to shocks related to the changing climate, boost rural livelihoods and enhance food security for about 728,000 people.

In a statement, the ADB said these included a $208m concessional loan for the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Resilient Irrigated Agriculture Livelihoods Development Project that will help scale up agricultural productivity and increase incomes for smallholder farmers in Nowshera, Swabi, and Upper Chitral districts through resilient irrigation systems and modern agricultural technologies.

Additionally, the project would provide livelihoods training for women, while supporting measures to increase the role of women in water governance, it said.

The statement said that another $260m concessional loan for the Integrated Hill Torrent Management Project would help mitigate flash flood risks and enhance floodwater harvesting in hilly areas of Punjab.

“The project in KP will construct and rehabilitate irrigation systems to be more resilient to disasters,” the statement said.

It added that the project would introduce modern water management practices, provide capacity-building activities for farmers and promote smart agricultural technologies.

“The project in Punjab will bolster flood resilience by building critical water management infrastructure for water retention, drainage, and flood protection,” the statement said.

It emphasised that the project would also promote sustainable agricultural practices including spate irrigation, as well as nature-based solutions that use floodwater as a resource to improve community water access, recharge aquifers, and restore ecosystems.

“The projects will not only safeguard communities from the adverse impacts of natural hazards, advance provincial disaster preparedness, but also increase agricultural yields, create more jobs, and provide a reliable water source for agriculture, community consumption, and ecosystem restoration,” the statement concluded.

ADB Country Director for Pakistan Emma Fan was quoted as saying that these projects would significantly contribute to strengthening food security, while responding to growing environmental pressures and the impacts of the changing climate.

“Resilient water management infrastructure and sustainable farming practices are vital for the economic potential of rural communities in these two provinces,” she stated.

The federal government approved the two projects last month. Valued at Rs69.893bn, the KP Resilient Irrigated Agriculture Livelihoods Development Project aims to rehabilitate the Pehur Main Canal, construct the Mulkhow Irrigation Distribution System and extend the Pehur High Level Canal.

The ADB will contribute Rs56.133bn ($200 million), while the provincial government will provide Rs11.692bn, along with land acquisition.

The federal government also recommended the Integrated Hill Torrent Management (Chachar–Mithawan) project in the districts of Dera Ghazi Khan and Rajanpur to the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council.

The project is estimated to cost Rs85.342bn, with the ADB contributing Rs73.060bn ($260m) and the Punjab government providing Rs12.282bn.

The project aims to introduce modern spate irrigation systems, flood-protection channels, telemetry systems and centralised supervisory control and data acquisition monitoring to strengthen regional water security.

articles.title: What is Modi's automated takedown law, which has embroiled Meta in a political storm?
articles.summary:
Meta’s content restrictions in India surged more than 130-fold in the first half of this year after a new government rule meant single takedown orders initiated an automated sweep to root out copies, embroiling the US company in a political battle with the Congress opposition party.

Congress’ youth wing has sued Meta and the government in an Indian court to strike down the rule, alleging that the automated system the company has deployed is wiping out the party’s social media footprint by blocking political posts including those carrying the name or photograph of party leader Rahul Gandhi.

The party has also staged massive protests outside Meta offices, accusing the company of acting in the interests of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), in what has become one of the Facebook and Instagram parent’s biggest challenges in its largest market by users.

How has Modi’s content takedown regime become stricter?

For years, only India’s IT and broadcasting ministries and courts could order content to be removed, and only on narrow grounds such as national security and public order.

In 2023, the government let federal and state agencies, including the police, send takedown notices for content barred under any law. And in 2024, Modi’s government launched a website, called Sahyog, which channels those notices to platforms.

Elon Musk’s X has been locked in a court dispute with Modi’s government over that website, which the social media company calls a “censorship portal”.

The latest dispute has arisen from critical changes to India’s IT law made in February: social media platforms must remove content deemed unlawful by an authority within three hours rather than 36, and big tech platforms such as YouTube, X and Meta must deploy technical measures such as “automated tools” to find “exactly identical” content and remove it.

The changed law also requires “appropriate human oversight” and periodic review of the automated tools for accuracy and bias. Platforms that fail to comply risk losing “safe harbour”, the legal protection that shields them from liability for what users post.

The digital rights group Internet Freedom Foundation has criticised the new system, saying that “censorship by automation is still censorship”.

How have content takedowns surged in India?

Meta’s online disclosures show it restricted access to 5.44 million items of content in India in the first half of 2026, about 130 times the 41,357 restricted in the previous six months. It restricted nearly 70,000 items in the whole of 2025.

These include Facebook and Instagram posts and accounts. Meta attributes the jump to automated detection of “100 per cent identical copies” under Indian law, not to an increase in the volume of legal requests.

Meta’s numbers also remain high as it has more than 500m users in India. Google’s online disclosures show it received formal requests for more than 65,000 pieces of content in India between January and June 2026, the highest ever, but it does not provide details on use of any automated tools. X’s website does not disclose the latest data on content removal requests received from the Indian government.

These numbers do not include actions that social media platforms take against content for breach of internal content guidelines.

How do Meta’s numbers in India compare to other countries?

India and Indonesia are among the “limited” countries where Meta says it is obliged to restrict content automatically and at scale under local law. Together they accounted for about 96pc of the 27.1m items Meta restricted in specific countries between January and June this year.

Meta’s 5.44m content restrictions in India were second only to Indonesia, where the number stood at 20.6m, but the company says over 20 million of Indonesia’s were “for alleged violation of local laws on gambling”.

And unlike India, where Meta’s restriction numbers in the period were the highest ever, Indonesia’s numbers have been falling over time.

articles.title: PM calls for effective guidance, simplified procedures for SMEs seeking financial support
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday called for better guidance for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) seeking financing from banks, enabling access to loans through simplified procedures.

Presiding over a meeting on facilitating access to credit for SMEs, the premier termed these enterprises the “backbone” of the country’s economy.

“Facilitating them will boost economic activity, employment and business opportunities,” the prime minister said.

The prime minister directed the provision of effective guidance and support to SMEs to improve their access to financial resources, prepare business documentation and benefit from opportunities in the export sector.

He called for further simplification of the procedures for SMEs to obtain loans.

“SMEs with export data available through the Pakistan Single Window, or those integrated into supply chains through Exim Insurance and digital invoicing, should be considered for loans against these records as collateral,” the prime minister said.

He also directed that banks consider SMEs’ cash flows as an alternative measure of collateral for lending.

PM Shehbaz called for a review of prudential regulations governing bank lending to SMEs. He further directed that banks be granted access to relevant data held by government institutions to expedite the lending process for these companies.

To facilitate SMEs, banks should not only provide loans but also assist them in issuing letters of credit (LCs) and providing bank guarantees, the PM said at the meeting. He added that banks achieving their prescribed SME lending targets would be encouraged.

The meeting was informed that banks were taking steps to strengthen their institutional capacity to accelerate lending to SMEs. The banks expressed their commitment to achieving a target of providing Rs2 trillion in loans to SMEs by June 2028 and increasing the number of SME borrowers to 775,000.

The target includes the disbursement of Rs886bn in new loans and the provision of financial facilities to 449,000 new borrowers.

Federal ministers Rana Tanveer Hussain, Ahsan Khan Cheema and Riaz Hussain Pirzada; PM’s Adviser Haroon Akhtar; Minister of State for Finance Bilal Azhar Kiyani; State Bank Governor Jameel Ahmad; chief executive officers of the National Bank of Pakistan, Bank Alfalah and the Bank of Punjab; and senior officials of relevant institutions attended the meeting.

Last week, PM Shehbaz approved the establishment of facilitation centres for SMEs at the district level, with pilot projects in Lahore, Peshawar, Karachi and Quetta.

In October, he directed authorities to increase financing for SMEs from Rs1.1tr to Rs2.2tr by 2028, citing their potential to drive economic growth and create business opportunities across the country.

articles.title: Hackers breach US Air Force flagship Cloud One computing platform
articles.summary:
Hackers have breached the US Air Force’s flagship cloud computing platform, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters, in a development that could jeopardise a vast swathe of sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data.

The intrusion at Cloud One was discovered within the past month or so during work to upgrade the system, two of the people said, adding that the discovery has led to disruption across the platform. Reuters could not establish the identity of the hackers, the full scope of the intrusion or whether any data had been stolen.

In a statement to Reuters, the Air Force said it “does not comment on the security posture, vulnerabilities or operational status of specific networks and systems. We continuously take prudent measures to protect Department (of the Air Force) information, systems and mission capabilities.”

A one-stop shop

Initiated in 2017, Cloud One was meant to serve as a one-stop shop for the Air Force’s IT needs, combining the resources of four operators Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle and Alphabet to power scores of applications, including ones that manage personnel data and pay or logistics and maintenance.

Among them are the Air Force’s Cloud-Based Command and Control, which collates air defence radar and other data feeds from across North America, and the Theatre Integrated Combat Munitions System, which tracks bombs and missiles across more than 200 US Air Force locations around the world.

SAIC was the prime contractor for Cloud One until 2025, when Leidos took over. SAIC did not respond to a request seeking comment. Leidos referred questions to the Air Force.

Cloud One is among the US military’s biggest cloud platforms, according to two of the sources.

“A breach here is a big deal,” one of the sources said. Investigators have called in Cyber Command, the US military’s cyber force, to assess the damage, one of the sources said.

Cyber Command did not respond to requests for comment.

A range of disruption

The discovery of the hack led to a range of disruption. Two of the sources, along with a fourth person familiar with the matter, said that efforts to migrate back-office applications to Cloud One, a longstanding military priority, have been paused.

Updates to applications already running on Cloud One were blocked, leaving Air Force personnel unable to apply fixes just as a new batch of serious software vulnerabilities has been disclosed across the technology industry. A fifth source said that some users had their administrator rights revoked.

All five sources spoke on condition of anonymity.

One source said that the cyber intruders exploited a software vulnerability to reach the control plane. That person likened the control plane to a universal remote, as intruders in theory could leverage their access to check the operational status of military aircraft or the movement of spare parts, though it was unclear whether the hackers did so in this case.

Reuters could not identify the specific vulnerability exploited by the hackers.

String of hacks

News of the breach comes amid heightened anxiety over AI-powered intrusions, a particularly serious problem for cloud-based networks because of the ability of AI models to swiftly detect weaknesses across wide surface areas.

The US government already has been dealing with the fallout from at least six other recently disclosed cyber incidents, including two at the FBI, a previous hack of Pentagon data, a recent leak of Department of Homeland Security personnel information, a breach affecting at least two spy agencies and a hack at the Treasury Department.

Cloud One has long been in the crosshairs of hackers.

In a 2023 commentary carried by the online publication FedScoop, Cloud One’s leadership touted what they called a “100 per cent success rate” in beating back what they said was a “staggering” number of attempts to penetrate the platform.

“There is no room for error when it comes to security,” Cloud One’s leadership wrote.

articles.title: Pakistan seeks deeper cooperation with IAEA on nuclear security
articles.summary:
Pakistan looks forward to further deepening cooperation with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) and international partners in support of sustainable nuclear security, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Friday.

The statement came as the 15th annual meeting of the International Network for Nuclear Security Training and Support Centres (NSSC Network), hosted by Pakistan in collaboration with the IAEA, concluded in Islamabad.

The meeting, held from Nov 23 to 26, brought together international delegates to discuss nuclear security training, capacity building and cooperation, the statement added.

A special event was also held at the headquarters of the Pakistan Nuclear Regulatory Authority (PNRA) to mark 20 years of Pakistan-IAEA cooperation in nuclear security. The event featured an exhibition of indigenous nuclear security technologies developed by Pakistan’s national industry.

Delegates also visited the Pakistan Institute of Engineering and Applied Sciences (PIEAS), where they were briefed on the country’s capabilities in nuclear engineering, research, education and training.

The programme included technical sessions, expert discussions and thematic presentations on emerging nuclear security challenges, institutional sustainability, human resource development and the future of international cooperation in nuclear security training.

At the concluding session, the chairman of the Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission (PAEC) underscored the importance of sustained international cooperation in strengthening nuclear security.

The IAEA’s unit head of the Division of Nuclear Security commended Pakistan for hosting the meeting, describing it as an important milestone in international nuclear security cooperation.

The statement said the meeting had provided a platform for member states to exchange expertise, strengthen national capabilities and identify future priorities.

Pakistan first hosted the NSSC Network’s annual meeting in 2016. Its return to Pakistan after a decade reflected the country’s sustained engagement with the IAEA and continued contribution to international nuclear security cooperation, the statement added.

In a video address at the opening session on Monday, IAEA Director General Rafael Mariano Grossi thanked Pakistan for hosting the meeting and highlighted the network’s role in translating nuclear security principles into practice.

A day earlier, Pakistan had called for keeping decisions on the use of nuclear weapons under human control and cautioned against the use of artificial intelligence (AI) systems to target nuclear command, control and communications systems.

Speaking at an open debate of the UN Security Council, Pakistan’s Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Syed Haider Shah, said emerging technologies posed new challenges to international security and called for appropriate safeguards, regulations and confidence-building measures to prevent miscalculation and escalation.

articles.title: FO says reports of boat carrying Pakistani migrants capsizing off Libya remain unverified
articles.summary:
The Foreign Office said on Friday that there had been no “independent verification” of the reports of a boat carrying Pakistani migrants capsizing off the coast of Libya and that Pakistan’s embassy in Libya was “actively pursuing the matter” to ascertain facts.

It was reported earlier this week that at least 25 people from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Bajaur district were feared dead or missing after a migrant boat capsized near Libya.

According to reports, the victims’ families said they had received information from the agents who arranged the travel that a migrant boat en route to Europe had reportedly capsized in the Mediterranean Sea near Libya on Nov 21.

While there has been no official confirmation of the incident, the funeral prayers in absentia of several individuals have been offered.

The FO said in its statement that Pakistan’s embassy in Tripoli was pursuing the matter to ascertain facts, including the presence of Pakistani nationals on the reportedly capsized boat.

“The embassy has contacted the relevant Libyan government authorities, the International Organisation for Migration, and other relevant stakeholders.

“Further information will be shared as soon as verified details become available,” the FO statement said.

Previous boat tragedies

In April this year, more than 80 migrants including 20 Pakistanis were reported missing after a boat carrying around 120 people capsized in the Central Mediterranean after departing from Libya.

Most of the missing Pakistanis had travelled to Libya posing as Umrah pilgrims, while others were on visit visas to Azerbaijan, Egypt and Uganda.

Following the boat tragedy, the FIA intensified its crackdown on human smuggling networks, targeting agents operating illegal overland routes through Iran and Turkiye. The agency also launched investigations to trace the suspects’ assets and sought Interpol’s assistance in pursuing agents based abroad.

In October last year, 18 migrants were killed when a wooden vessel capsized off the coast of Libya, while 64 people, including 12 Pakistanis, were reported missing. The boat capsized off Surman due to high waves, only a few hours after setting sail.

In April 2025, four Pakistanis were among the 11 migrants found dead in a shipwreck near Libya’s Harawa coast.

In June 2023, at least 209 Pakistanis were among the migrants aboard an overloaded fishing boat that capsized and sank in international waters off Greece on June 14.

Witnesses estimated that between 400 and 750 people were aboard the vessel. The official death toll stood at 82, while 104 people survived, including 12 Pakistanis.

articles.title: Quetta Gladiators dismiss sale rumours, reaffirm commitment to PSL
articles.summary:
Quetta Gladiators have dismissed speculation about a possible sale of the franchise or an exit from the Pakistan Super League (PSL), reaffirming their financial stability and commitment to the competition.

In a statement issued on Friday, the franchise said rumours circulating on social media and in some media reports had been “taken out of context, misconstrued or were entirely without foundation”.

It added that remarks attributed to owner Nadeem Omar in a recent interview did not accurately reflect the franchise’s financial position.

“Over its history, Quetta Gladiators has been one of the most profitable franchises in the Pakistan Super League,” the statement said, adding that the team had recorded annual profits since the league’s fourth season and completed its first decade among the competition’s most financially successful franchises.

Nadeem reaffirmed his confidence in the PSL, describing it as a pillar of world cricket with one of the largest fan bases globally.

He also welcomed the recent direct signings of international players by PSL franchises, including New Zealand fast bowler Lockie Ferguson by Quetta Gladiators, describing the developments as evidence of the league’s growing strength.

The statement also highlighted the decision to stage the opening ceremony of the 12th PSL season in Peshawar, calling it a positive sign of the competition’s expanding reach across the country.

“Our passion for Quetta Gladiators, a labour of love built on years of effort, is greater than ever,” the statement said.

The owner also rejected suggestions that financial pressure or health concerns were behind speculation about a possible sale, adding that a change of ownership would only be considered if an offer was received that “cannot be refused”.

The franchise thanked the Pakistan Cricket Board, PSL management, commercial partners and supporters for their continued backing, expressing confidence that Quetta Gladiators would remain in safe hands.

The clarification follows reports earlier this month suggesting that the franchise could be put up for sale ahead of PSL 12, scheduled to take place from March to May 2027. Some reports had also cited a possible valuation of around Rs3 billion.

In earlier interviews, Nadeem had indicated that it could be the right time to part ways with the PSL if a suitable offer and certain conditions were met.

He had pointed to the commercial challenges of competing with the Indian Premier League, limited local sponsorship and merchandising opportunities, as well as the overlapping schedules of the two leagues since 2025.

He had, however, stressed that any discussions were preliminary and that the franchise’s identity and its association with Quetta and Balochistan remained important considerations.

No sale or transaction has been announced or finalised.

Quetta Gladiators were among the original franchises when the PSL was launched in 2016. The team reached the final in its first two seasons before winning its maiden title in 2019 under Sarfaraz Ahmed, defeating Peshawar Zalmi. They finished runners-up again in 2025.

The franchise also renewed its rights for the 2026-2035 cycle in late 2025 as part of the league’s restructured agreements.

articles.title: Fleeing murder suspect crashes into elephant in Sri Lanka
articles.summary:
A Sri Lankan man suspected of fatally stabbing a woman was arrested on Friday after he crashed his scooter into a wild elephant as he attempted to escape, police said.

The 49-year-old man is accused of stabbing the woman in her home in the northern district of Anuradhapura, a police official told AFP.

However, his attempted escape ended when his scooter crashed into the elephant as it emerged from the jungle onto the road a short distance away, the official said.

Witnesses told police the elephant appeared to be unharmed and retreated into the jungle.

The man was arrested and was receiving treatment for unspecified injuries under armed guard in hospital. Police also said they had recovered the suspected murder weapon.

Encounters between humans and elephants are relatively common in Sri Lanka, where expanding settlements and farms often overlap with animal habitats.

The island has recorded about 400 elephant and 150 human deaths annually over the past five years, according to official figures.

Sri Lanka is home to an estimated 7,000 wild elephants and considers the animals a national treasure and they are protected by law.

However, residents in remote villages sometimes attack elephants that destroy their crops.

articles.title: ECP says it cannot force parties to field women on winnable seats
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Friday made it clear that the allocation of party tickets was an internal matter for political parties and that it had no legal authority to intervene.

The ECP explained its position a day after a National Assembly panel directed it to ensure that the five per cent quota for women on general seats under Section 206 of the Elections Act, 2017, is implemented in a manner that women are fielded on seats where their victory is certain.

The ECP said it had informed the Sub-Committee of the National Assembly’s Special Committee on Gender Mainstreaming at the time that, under the existing electoral laws, the authority to award tickets to women rested with the political party concerned.

According to the commission, ‘‘it could neither interfere in the process of ticket distribution nor decide on which seat a party should field a woman candidate”.

The distribution of seats, the ECP said, was an internal affair of political parties. Therefore, if the committee wanted women to be given general seats where their victory was assured, legislation would be required for that purpose, and the power to legislate rested with Parliament.

Section 206 of the Elections Act, 2017, requires every political party to award at least five per cent of its tickets on general seats to women candidates.

The provision was introduced to increase women’s representation in elected bodies and ensure that parties do not confine women candidates to reserved seats alone.

In practice, however, women candidates have often been fielded on seats considered difficult for their parties, a concern repeatedly raised in Parliament and by civil society organisations.

The NA body has now urged the ECP to ensure that the quota translates into meaningful representation by requiring political parties to field women candidates in winnable constituencies.

The ECP’s position is that the existing law only prescribes a minimum percentage of tickets for women. It does not empower the commission to assess the winnability of a constituency or direct a party to change its candidate for a particular seat.

Legal experts say any such condition would require an amendment to the Elections Act by Parliament, specifying criteria for winnable seats and the mechanism for enforcement.

The committee also directed the ECP to make arrangements for filling 563 vacant seats in various local governments.

In this regard, the ECP informed the committee that it had issued election schedules on several occasions to fill these vacant seats.

However, no woman had filed nomination papers for these seats, the commission said, adding that elections could not be held in the absence of candidates.

The ECP said it remained ready to hold elections on vacant seats as soon as candidates came forward in accordance with the law.

At Thursday’s meeting, the committee also reviewed a briefing by Nadra and noted that female registrations in 2026 were 5.57pc higher than male registrations. However, Senator Qaim Khani raised concerns over women’s representation in the authority’s senior management, where only 15 women held positions of director or above.

articles.title: Islamabad police announce road closures, traffic diversions ahead of foreign delegations' arrival
articles.summary:
Ahead of the arrival of foreign delegations in the federal capital on Friday, Islamabad police issued traffic advisories outlining road closures and alternative routes for commuters.

The district administration also previously declared Friday a local holiday in the twin cities.

Police said on Friday that entry and exit routes to and from the Red Zone, including those around Serena Hotel, Nadra Chowk, Ayub Chowk and Express Chowk, would remain closed from Thursday until 12:30am on Saturday.

Residents were advised to use Margalla Road to travel to and from the Red Zone during this period.

Police added that diversions would be in place at various locations along the Express Highway and Srinagar Highway on Friday.

Commuters travelling on Srinagar Highway were advised to use Suhrawardy Road, Service Road G-8, Service Road G-9 and Zero Point.

Traffic heading towards Faizabad should use Faisal Avenue, while commuters using Ninth Avenue should take Service Road East instead, police said.

Those travelling to Islamabad from Koral were advised to use Old Airport, Rawal Road, Rawalpindi-Murree Road, IJP Road and Faqir Appi Road.

Police said commuters should use Lehtrar Road and Park Road if the Koral Express Highway, Murree Road and Club Road were closed.

Drivers heading to the New Islamabad International Airport and Peshawar Road were advised to use Jinnah Avenue and Margalla Road, police said. Those travelling to Islamabad from Bani Gala should use Bani Gala Road and Park Road.

Police also warned that traffic on the highways would remain slow while diversions were in place. Commuters were advised to allow an additional 20 to 25 minutes for their journeys.

Islamabad police advised residents to call 1915 for traffic information and guidance, adding that the latest traffic updates would be available on Islamabad Traffic Police’s social media platforms.

Metro bus services were also expected to be partially suspended from Nov 26 to 28.

An earlier notification issued by the district magistrate’s office stated that Trail 3 and Trail 5 would remain closed to the public in the capital on Friday from 6am to 11pm.

Separately, a notice was issued regarding the expected partial suspension of the Rawalpindi-Islamabad Metro Bus Service from Thursday to Saturday due to “VIP movement”.

Moreover, the entry of heavy vehicles into Islamabad and Rawalpindi would be prohibited from 6pm on Thursday until 12:30am on Saturday. Heavy vehicles would not be allowed to enter the twin cities via the Motorway or GT Road, while the Faizabad Bus Terminal would remain closed during this period.

Additionally, metro bus and electric bus services operating between 7th Avenue Metro Station and Pak Secretariat would remain suspended from 10pm on Thursday until 12:30am on Saturday.

Strict security measures are also being put in place in the capital for the visiting delegations. The army will supervise security arrangements, while the Rangers and Islamabad police, including 2,000 officers, will also perform duties.

Deployment will also be made along the route from the airport to the Red Zone. All entry points to the Red Zone will be sealed. Only one entry point will be partially opened for security personnel, relevant authorities and officials.

articles.title: Major storm batters US on Thanksgiving holiday
articles.summary:
A powerful storm disrupted Thanksgiving celebrations for millions of Americans on Friday, as New York’s famed Macy’s parade was postponed for the first time in its 100-year history.

Heavy rain and strong winds from the “Nor-easter” battered the central and eastern United States, creating treacherous travel conditions during one of the country’s busiest holiday periods.

As families were gathering for traditional holiday feasts, more than 900,000 homes and businesses were without power, with Pennsylvania, Maryland and Virginia particularly hard hit, according to tracking website PowerOutage.

At airports, nearly 400 flights were cancelled and over 2,000 were delayed in the United States, mostly in the East, figures from FlightAware showed.

A person walks in front of the Manhattan Bridge and East River during a Thanksgiving Day storm in the Brooklyn Borough of New York City, US on November 26, 2026. —Reuters

New York’s famed parade, which sees brightly coloured balloons travel through the heart of Manhattan, was pushed back to Saturday due to what organisers said was an “abundance of caution.” Millions of people typically gather to catch a glimpse of the festivities.

The only other time the parade was not held on Thanksgiving Thursday was when it was cancelled for three years during World War II.

Organisers would have been only too aware of the gusting winds that wrecked the parade back in 1997 when a careening 18-foot figure of the “Cat in the Hat” toppled a lamppost, knocking one bystander unconscious.

“While we are heartbroken that our parade was postponed, the safety of our partners, the safety of our participants — and spectators — is and always will be our top priority,” said Macy’s parade executive producer Will Coss.

Stay safe

While flooding was reported up and down the East Coast, impacts were also felt inland, with powerful gusts and inundated soil leading to trees tumbling over onto power lines and homes.

Authorities in the Maryland suburbs of the US capital, worried about the impact of power outages on the water treatment network, asked nearly two million customers to conserve tap water consumption.

Officials urged people to limit road travel, while several major bridges were closed due to high winds.

People visit the Lincoln Memorial amidst a rain storm in Washington, DC, US on November 26, 2026. —Reuters

New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill, who declared a state of emergency Wednesday over the weather, urged residents to take precautions to stay safe.

“Keep your devices charged, report power outages directly to your utility provider, and stay away from downed power lines,” she wrote on X.

Some people improvised to still enjoy Thanksgiving, which is traditionally marked by gathering with family around a large meal, with turkey as the centerpiece.

“No electricity? No problem,” celebrity chef Jose Andres wrote on X, alongside a video of a candlelit dining room and lobsters cooking on a gas-powered stove.

The east coast disruption came as Californians also suffered weather woes this week with massive waves battering the coast, prompting evacuations in some areas and soaking San Francisco.

articles.title: India-US trade agreement nearing completion: Indian commerce minister
articles.summary:
India said Friday it was close to finalising a long-awaited trade deal with the United States after Washington proposed higher tariffs on the country’s goods if negotiations fail.

“The US trade deal is close to culmination,” Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal told an industry conference, adding that differences were beginning to be resolved.

“The process and pathway, which was always something which held back finalising the deal, is now taking some shape,” he said.

Goyal’s comments came after US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer on Wednesday said Indian goods would face tariffs of 17 per cent if a trade deal is reached but rise to as much as 25pc if not.

The new tariffs face a period of public consultation process before taking effect next year.

The United States is India’s largest trading partner and the two have been negotiating a trade deal since reaching an interim accord in February.

New Delhi has sought access to the US market for key export sectors including textiles, pharmaceuticals and engineering goods, while Washington has pushed for greater access for American products and closer alignment on trade rules.

Since February, several rounds of talks have taken place but have been complicated by Washington launching a probe into unfair trade practices against multiple countries, including India.

Last month, New Delhi’s Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said trade deal talks between India and US had reached a “plateau”, after negotiations dragged on for months with the sides struggling to resolve sticking points.

On Wednesday, the US unveiled proposed tariffs on 14 economies, including India, after a months-long probe into alleged excess production. The duties, proposed at up to 20pc, came over allegations that the economies “are promoting production and capacity divorced from the realities of demand and market principles,” a senior US official said on condition of anonymity.

articles.title: Erdogan completes Turkiye's ratification of Makkah defence pact
articles.summary:
President Tayyip Erdogan has formally approved the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, the country’s Official Gazette said on Friday, completing Turkiye’s ratification after parliament ratified it earlier this month.

Turkiye’s parliament ratified the agreement on November 5, paving the way for Ankara to support Riyadh amid attacks by Yemen’s Houthi militia against the kingdom. Under the agreement, an attack on one party constitutes an attack on all.

The approval comes as Pakistan hosts a two-day meeting of the tripartite alliance’s top decision-making body from Friday, with discussions also expected to feature the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi fighters.

The third session of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) is being held in Islamabad, where authorities have announced a public holiday and imposed special movement restrictions for the high-level gathering. A local holiday has also been announced in Rawalpindi.

The meeting is expected to focus on finalising standard operating procedures (SOPs), establishing an implementation mechanism and defining coordination between the three countries’ political, defence and military institutions, a Pakistani official said.

Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said on Thursday that the foreign and defence ministers of Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan would participate in the meeting, adding that the “continuous turmoil south of Saudi Arabia will obviously be one agenda point in the meeting”.

A ruling party lawmaker told Reuters last month that Turkiye would also submit a mandate to parliament seeking approval for the deployment of military personnel to Saudi Arabia under the agreement.

Ankara’s ratification clears another step towards the implementation of the pact, which could allow Turkiye to provide military support to Riyadh amid attacks by Houthis against the kingdom.

The alliance

The three countries signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement on Aug 7. The pact provides that an armed attack on any one member will be considered an attack on all, obliging the other two to extend assistance through available means, including military support.

The SPDC, which brings together the foreign and defence ministers and chiefs of defence staff of the three countries, is the alliance’s principal decision-making forum.

A permanent secretariat has been established in Riyadh to coordinate its work, with Pakistan’s retired Lt Gen Nauman Mahmood appointed as its first secretary general for a three-year term. A working committee comprising officials from member countries is also functioning.

Turkiye’s ratification of the agreement has completed the accession process for all three member states.

The alliance has yet to publicly define its doctrine, the composition of forces, command arrangements or procedures governing a collective military response.

An emergency SPDC meeting in Riyadh on Oct 5 had called for moving towards practical implementation of collective defence commitments, including arrangements for the rapid deployment of agreed forces and capabilities, subject to national laws.

Wider regional tensions

The alliance’s formation also comes against the backdrop of wider regional tensions involving Iran, the United States and Israel.

While the three members share an interest in strengthening regional deterrence, their differing strategic priorities make it important to define the alliance’s scope without allowing it to become an instrument for wider military confrontation.

Asif declined to comment on how the alliance would respond to a direct Iranian attack on Saudi Arabia, but identified Israel as a possible threat to other countries in the region.

“The possibility of some conflict, or aggression from the Israeli side exists, so we need to close our ranks, the countries of this region,” he said.

Managing relations with Iran will be particularly important for Pakistan, which has sought to preserve diplomatic engagement with Tehran while deepening defence cooperation with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.

A meeting in Tehran involving representatives of the three countries and Iranian officials, held on Pakistan’s initiative, reflected efforts to keep channels of communication open between the two sides.

Pakistan brokered a June accord that led to a brief halt in fighting between the US and Iran and laid out a roadmap for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and negotiations on Tehran’s nuclear programme.

However, the truce collapsed, with Washington and Tehran accusing each other of violating the agreement, prompting months of shuttle diplomacy led principally by Qatar and Pakistan.

Asif said Pakistan had played “a very, very constructive role” between Washington and Tehran, but the outcome of ongoing mediation was “still fragile” and peace was “not yet embedded in a way people were expecting”.

Turkiye had earlier stressed the defensive character of the agreement and remained cautious about involvement in combat operations in Yemen.

articles.title: LHC seeks replies on plea by five Afghan medical students over MBBS registration
articles.summary:
LAHORE: The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Friday issued notices to the Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) and other respondents on a petition filed by five Afghan medical students seeking registration to sit their first professional MBBS examination in January.

The petitioners — Forough Dihqanpur, Shahira Sharif, Zahra Nabawi, Faiza Noori and Shabana Rahimi — are enrolled in the first year of the MBBS programme at Sheikh Khalifa Bin Zayed Al Nahyan Medical and Dental College, Lahore, under the Allama Muhammad Iqbal Scholarship Programme run by the Higher Education Commission (HEC).

Advocate Asad Jamal, counsel for the petitioners, informed the court that they joined the college on April 6 after undergoing a multi-stage selection process conducted by the HEC. They were subsequently issued student cards and bona fide certificates, he added.

He argued that registration is a mandatory prerequisite for appearing in the first professional examination, scheduled to be held from Jan 4 to 11, 2027.

He pointed out that the college has asked the University of Health Sciences (UHS) to open its registration portal for the students, but the university has declined, saying the PMDC has not permitted such admissions for the 2025-26 session.

The counsel further said that the PMDC subsequently approved the placement of 68 nominated Afghan students in public-sector colleges beyond the approved intake.

Relying on Regulations 6 and 7 of the PMDC’s 2025 admissions regulations, he argued that the affiliating university was required to verify and register admitted students and that UHS could not withhold a decision indefinitely.

He asked the court to declare the inaction unlawful and direct the respondents to complete the petitioners’ registration. He also sought provisional registration in the interim to enable them to sit the examination.

However, Justice Asim Hafeez issued notices to the respondents, directing them to submit their replies by Dec 1 to the main petition and the application for interim relief.

The petition named the PMDC, UHS, the Punjab government, the college, the federal government, the health ministry and the HEC as respondents.

In September, the LHC suspended the operation of PMDC directives ordering Afghan medical students to return to Afghanistan. The order came after 13 Afghan students, including seven women and six men, enrolled at different medical colleges in Lahore, challenged the directives.

The PMDC barred medical and dental colleges from admitting or placing Afghan students for the current academic session and said those already enrolled in such programmes were required to return to Afghanistan.

In October, the LHC extended its stay against the expulsion and deportation of Afghan medical students and granted the PMDC more time to submit its reply.

Separately, the Peshawar High Court (PHC) temporarily restrained the deportation of 86 Afghan students enrolled in public-sector medical colleges in the province and allowed them to continue their studies.

articles.title: Makers step up rollout of electric bikes
articles.summary:
KARACHI: Amid the falling trend in petrol prices, a growing number of stakeholders have stepped up efforts to test their new electric bikes in the market.

But some assemblers are still enjoying robust sales of petrol-run bikes. For instance, Atlas Honda posted record sales of 173,152 units last month, jacking up the aggregate to 643,561 units in 4MFY27 from 505,269 units. It was followed by United Motorcycle, with sales rising to 82,474 from 56,519 in the same period.

Millat Tractors Ltd (MTL) is set to launch its EV two-wheelers on Nov 29. It has already designated its dealers and production is underway.

According to Topline Securities, MTL said at a corporate briefing that it plans to introduce five lithium-ion-powered models, including bikes and scooters.

Millat Industrial, a subsidiary of MTL, will manufacture the electric two-wheelers, with an annual production capacity of 250,000 units.

ICMAP urges focus on domestic EV industry instead of subsidising purchase

Initially, five or six variants of both bike and scooty will be launched.

Air Link Communication Limited had launched its AirV EV bikes on Nov 4 with an annual production capacity of 100,000 at Sundar Green Special Economic Zone.

The management plans to scale up output gradually and has set a target of importing 10,000-15,000 units and will place further orders based on market response.

Topline Securities, while revealing this information from Air Link’s corporate briefing, said the prices of its bikes would range between Rs200,000 and Rs500,000. The firm does not intend to sell the product on credit.

Subsidy on purchase of bikes

The Punjab government has decided to provide a subsidy of Rs50,000 for the purchase of electric bikes, while the Pakistan Accelerated Vehicle Electrification programme (PAVE) has also offered a subsidy of Rs80,000.

Mohammad Sabir Shaikh, an expert on bikes, said assemblers are testing their luck in the electric market. The current prices of EV bikes range between Rs170,000 and Rs700,000.

The sale of EV bikes has hit over 300,000 over the past 12 months, with Punjab leading other regions in the number of units sold. The Karachi market is showing a moderate growth, Sabir Shaikh added.

Urgency of transition

According to an analysis by the Institute of Cost and Management Accountants of Pakistan (ICMAP), titled “Can PAVE shift Pakistan from EV adoption to EV industry”, the urgency of this transition is underscored by volatile fuel prices.

The analysis observes that the country’s electric vehicle transition should move beyond subsidising vehicle purchases towards building a domestic EV industry, or risk replacing dependence on imported petroleum with dependence on imported electric vehicles, batteries and related technologies.

Under the New Energy Vehicle (NEV) Policy 2025-30, it is envisaged that Pakistan Accelerated Vehicle Electri­fication Programme (PAVE) will accelerate electric mobility through subsidies, financing and vehicle distribution.

The programme’s first two phases envisage the distribution of approximately 116,000 electric bikes. Despite the latest decline, the price has remained almost 20 per cent higher than at the beginning of March, illustrating the country’s vulnerability to international petroleum market volatility, import costs and foreign-exchange pressures.

The ICMAP advises that PAVE should be positioned not merely as a vehicle subsidy scheme, but as a strategic economic instrument linking energy security, household affordability and industrial competitiveness.

However, the analysis highlights the gap between generating demand and translating it into vehicles on the road. During the initial phase, banks received 44,689 applications by May 31, but they processed only 9,889, or merely 22pc, of these.

Approval was granted in just 4,075 cases, representing just 9pc of the total number of applications, while 34,800, or 78pc, remained unprocessed.

Financing provided at that stage amounted to Rs143 million, while 5,409 vehicles were reported as distributed, the analysis said.

Published in Dawn, November 27th, 2026

articles.title: 26th, 27th Amendments sparked judicial conflict: ex-IHC judge
articles.summary:
• Kayani calls for parliamentary intervention to resolve judicial conflict
• Urges authorities not to issue notices to media under Peca

ISLAMABAD: Former Islam­abad High Court (IHC) judge reti­red Justice Mohsin Akhtar Kayani has said that the 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments have triggered a conflict between two superior courts, warning that the disregard for established judicial precedents and the creation of new ones have further complicated the constitutional and legal framework.

Speaking at a seminar titled ‘Personal Safety and Justice in a Digital World’, organised by the Institute of Regional Studies in Islamabad, Justice Kayani said that the issues arising from the Nadia Sarwar case before the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) could only be addressed through parliament.

He said the current state of the Constitution was evident to everyone, yet people remained silent despite being aware of what was happening.

“The 26th and 27th amendments have given rise to a conflict between two superior courts,” he said, adding that established judicial precedents were being disregarded and new, problematic precedents were being set.

He said parliament was the appropriate forum for resolving conflicts between the superior courts, emphasising that legislation was its prerogative, while the interpretation of the Constitution was the responsibility of the courts.

He urged lawmakers to debate legal matters in parliament before introducing legislation to ensure that parliamentarians fully understood the laws being enacted and their implications.

The former judge also questioned the growing use of laws regulating online expression, particularly the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca), saying that journalists, members of parliament and lawyers were among those affected by the legislation.

He urged the authorities not to issue notices to media organisations under Section 26-A merely for publishing news reports.

“For God’s sake, do not issue notices to the media under Section 26-A. It should not be the case that the moment the media reports a story, a notice is im-mediately issued against them,”

he said, stressing the need to protect journalists.

He questioned the effectiveness of establishing new agencies to enforce such laws, remarking that authorities often created new agencies only to appoint the same officers under different uniforms.

He also pointed out that several terms associated with online harassment remained poorly understood, adding that those for whom the legislation was intended had neither been properly consulted nor adequately informed about its provisions.

Published in Dawn, November 27th, 2026

articles.title: Friday Sermon: Zoning, rotational presidency between the north and the south, By Murtadha Gusau
articles.summary:
In the Name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the Worlds, who fashioned humanity into diverse nations and tribes so that we may know, honour, and uplift one another. articles.title: As Africa Prepares for the 10th FOCAC Conference in Congo
articles.summary:
By Abdulrahman B. Dambazau

As Africa prepares for the next Forum on China–Africa Cooperation, the question before us is how this partnership can improve the lives and security of our people. African citizens should be able to see its value in functioning health services, productive enterprises, reliable electricity and better opportunities for their children.

The Republic of the Congo will host the 10th FOCAC Ministerial Conference in 2027 and, as the African co-chair of FOCAC for 2024–2027, will co-chair the meeting with China. The conference offers an opportunity to assess existing commitments and shape the next phase of cooperation. Africa should arrive with a coordinated agenda, credible projects and clear expectations of what successful implementation would mean.

The Beijing Action Plan for 2025–2027 already provides a broad framework, encompassing industrial development, trade, agriculture, healthcare, green development and common security. Our preparation should connect these priorities around a common purpose: building African capacity to sustain development.

That preparation should begin with a candid review. Participating countries should establish which commitments have become agreements, which agreements have secured financing and which projects are operating. These distinctions matter. A signed memorandum can create an opportunity, but its value depends on the investment, services or employment that follow.

Such a review should be undertaken constructively with Chinese partners, recognising achievements and identifying obstacles. Where progress has stalled, both sides should agree on corrective action, responsible institutions and realistic deadlines. This would give the next round of commitments a firmer foundation.

Africa’s central economic priority should be the capacity to produce competitively. Cooperation should help African enterprises process agricultural produce, develop manufacturing and add value to mineral resources where commercially and environmentally viable. Negotiations should address local suppliers, technology transfer and the skills needed to sustain operations.

Infrastructure should serve this productive purpose. An industrial park needs dependable electricity, water, transport and viable businesses. A processing plant needs reliable inputs and buyers. Investment proposals should bring these requirements together, with maintenance and operating costs considered from the outset.

Trade opportunities also require preparation. African producers need support to meet standards, obtain certification, package goods and fulfil orders consistently. The African Continental Free Trade Area should guide efforts to build regional supply chains, enabling neighbouring countries to develop complementary industries and share infrastructure. Access to the Chinese market should strengthen Africa’s capacity to trade within the continent as well.

Healthcare deserves a prominent place in this agenda. African countries should prioritise primary healthcare, maternal and child health, diagnostic services and affordable, quality medicines. Hospitals and equipment need trained personnel, reliable utilities, maintenance and recurrent funding. Success should be measured by whether people can obtain timely, effective care without financial hardship.

Partnerships should also develop pharmaceutical and vaccine manufacturing, strengthen laboratories and support medical research and specialist training. These investments should reinforce national institutions and the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention. Technology transfer must include quality assurance, regulatory capacity and procurement arrangements capable of sustaining production.

Public health cooperation should explicitly embrace One Health policies. The One Health approach recognises the interdependence of human, animal, plant and environmental health. It provides a practical basis for connecting healthcare with agriculture, food safety and environmental protection.

Through FOCAC, Africa should seek support for coordinated disease surveillance, shared laboratory capacity and joint emergency planning among health, veterinary, agricultural and environmental authorities. Priorities should include diseases transmitted between animals and humans, food safety and antimicrobial resistance, including responsible use of medicines in human and animal healthcare. Joint research and professional training should help institutions identify risks early and respond together.

Climate change should be equally central to the discussions in Congo. African priorities should include adaptation through flood protection, drought preparedness, water management, early warning systems and infrastructure designed to withstand changing climatic conditions. Each project should explain the risks it addresses, the communities it serves and how its operation will be funded.

Cooperation on renewable energy should support dependable supply and productive activity. Generation must be planned alongside transmission, distribution, storage and affordable connections. African countries should also seek opportunities to develop local technical expertise and participate in the industries supplying energy equipment and services.

Climate finance should reflect both affordability and public benefit. Accessible grants and concessional resources should support suitable adaptation projects, alongside private investment in commercially viable activities. African institutions need the expertise to prepare credible proposals, assess financing terms and monitor delivery.

The connection between climate and public health should receive particular attention. Cooperation should support preparedness for extreme heat, reliable water and sanitation, and health facilities able to continue operating during emergencies. One Health offers a useful framework for bringing these responsibilities together across institutions.

Agriculture provides another opportunity to combine livelihoods, health and resilience. Partnerships should cover irrigation, extension services, storage, processing and market access, with workable arrangements for smallholders, women and young entrepreneurs. Machinery must come with trained operators, spare parts and affordable maintenance.

Education and skills should support every part of this programme. Universities, polytechnics and vocational institutions should work with industry to prepare the professionals required by actual projects. Training should be assessed through competence and subsequent employment. Digital cooperation should build local capacity to maintain technology, protect information and govern its use.

Security must remain integral to these discussions. My experience in military leadership and public administration has reinforced the importance of effective security institutions, functioning justice systems and economic opportunity in sustaining peace. Investment needs protection, while communities need confidence that development will improve their lives.

FOCAC security cooperation should support African priorities in peacekeeping, professional training, maritime security and border management. Development projects should also address land acquisition, compensation and community grievances carefully. Local participation and accountable institutions can help protect the benefits of investment.

Africa must take responsibility for the quality of its preparation and delivery. Governments should strengthen project appraisal, procurement and financial oversight, while providing predictable rules and timely decisions. Financing should be selected according to each project’s needs, with proper assessment of repayment obligations, foreign exchange exposure and future operating costs.

Before Congo, each country should prepare a manageable portfolio of priorities, supported by feasibility work, financing proposals and responsible institutions. The African Union and regional bodies should help identify projects with wider benefits. Diplomatic missions, businesses and researchers should contribute evidence and maintain continuity from negotiation to implementation.

China is an important partner in Africa’s development. A stronger partnership will emerge from a clear African agenda and practical cooperation grounded in mutual benefit. The lasting measure of the next FOCAC should be the productive capacity, better health, climate resilience and greater security it helps African people achieve.

Abdulrahman B. Dambazau is a retired Lieutenant General, former Chief of Army Staff and former Minister of Interior. He is currently the Ambassador of the Federal Republic of Nigeria to the People’s Republic of China.

The post As Africa Prepares for the 10th FOCAC Conference in Congo appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: 2027: OK Movement announces withdrawal of support for Obi, Kwankwaso, NDC
articles.summary:
The OK Movement, a political support group previously associated with the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential ticket of Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso, has withdrawn its campaign and mobilisation support for the party ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The group said its decision followed what it described as the discontinuation of its political relationship with Obi and the NDC, adding that it would announce its preferred political party and presidential candidate in due course.

In a statement on Friday, the National Director-General of the OK Movement, John Ozyl Ughulu, said the group had formally been informed that Obi and the party had decided to end their political relationship with the movement.

He described the development as regrettable but said the group respected the decision, while expressing appreciation to Obi for the engagements and opportunities shared with the movement.

“Following this development, the National Leadership of the OK Movement has resolved to officially discontinue all campaign, mobilisation and operational support for the NDC Party, effective immediately,” the statement said.

The group added that all its political structures and operational engagements at ward, local government and state levels had been withdrawn from the NDC’s campaign and mobilisation activities.

It said the NDC had a considerable social media following which, if properly organised and translated into grassroots political participation, could deliver significant electoral benefits, adding that the responsibility for converting such support into electoral strength now rested with the party and its leadership.

Ughulu said the movement had commenced engagements with other political parties and presidential candidates whose political vision, leadership capacity and ideological commitments aligned with its principles and values.

“The OK Movement will, in due course, announce its preferred political party and presidential candidate for the 2027 general elections.

“We have already commenced engagements with other political parties and potential presidential candidates whose political vision, leadership capacity and ideological commitments align with our established principles and values,” he said.

The group said its organisational strength cut across wards, local governments and states, expressing confidence that its grassroots presence, reach and mobilisation capacity could make it a formidable independent political force capable of influencing the 2027 elections and challenging the present administration.

“Our data are clear. Our structures speak for us. Our ideology defines us. The OK Movement remains independent in its identity, organisational structure and political decisions. No individual, political party or political interest owns this movement,” it said.

The movement also said leadership should be defined by capacity, competence, integrity and the ability to resolve disagreements, build bridges and unite people rather than encourage division or exploit internal conflicts.

It reaffirmed its commitment to integrity, fairness, equity, justice, competence, accountability and national unity, insisting that the principles were non-negotiable and would not be compromised for political convenience.

The group urged members, coordinators and supporters to remain calm, disciplined and focused while awaiting further directives from its national leadership, adding that members were free to make their own political choices without intimidation or hostility.

It also expressed appreciation to members and volunteers for their sacrifices and commitment, assuring them that their efforts in building the movement across the country had not been in vain.

The post 2027: OK Movement announces withdrawal of support for Obi, Kwankwaso, NDC appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.
