articles.title: 2027: Odii vows to end poverty, industrialise Ebonyi
articles.summary:
The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Ebonyi State, Chief Ifeanyi Odii, has vowed to tackle poverty, industrialise the state and create jobs, accusing the incumbent administration of failing to turn increased federal allocations into improved living conditions.

Odii, who spoke on Thursday at the flag-off of the PDP governorship campaign in Abakaliki, said the state’s growing revenue had not translated into the level of development and welfare expected by its residents.

He argued that governance should be measured by its impact on the people, rather than the amount of money received or spent by government.

The PDP candidate identified poverty, poor rural roads, inadequate healthcare facilities, limited economic opportunities and lack of access to clean water as major challenges facing the state.

He claimed that available national assessments indicated that nearly eight out of every 10 residents of Ebonyi were living in multidimensional poverty.

Odii also faulted what he described as inadequate investment in agriculture, arguing that a state whose economy depended largely on farming could not justify allocating less than two per cent of its 2025 budget to the sector.

He questioned the utilisation of funds earmarked for education, particularly those meant for teachers’ training and children’s educational needs.

The candidate further expressed concern over Ebonyi’s weak industrial base despite its abundant mineral resources, noting that farmers continued to face difficulties while the state remained heavily dependent on federal allocations.

According to him, his administration, if elected, would prioritise industrialisation, economic diversification, job creation and accountable governance.

“The government must account for the resources entrusted to it and demonstrate the results it has achieved. Government must be measured by how much it has improved the lives of the people,” he said.

Odii, who recalled his participation in the 2023 governorship election, alleged that he was denied victory despite winning the poll.

He, however, expressed confidence that the 2027 election would provide another opportunity for residents to elect their preferred leaders, vowing that the PDP would resist any attempt to undermine its electoral mandate.

He said his experience in business, economic management and social responsibility had equipped him with the capacity to address the developmental challenges facing the state.

The rally attracted thousands of party supporters, stakeholders, women and youths from the 13 local government areas of the state.

The PDP National Chairman, Abdulrahman Muhammed, who attended the event alongside members of the party’s National Working Committee, presented the party’s flags to Odii, his running mate, Patrick Mgbebu, and other candidates.

Muhammed described the turnout as evidence of the party’s grassroots strength and acceptance in Ebonyi.

“Today, we are here in Ebonyi. Ebonyi is PDP, and PDP is Ebonyi,” he declared.

He urged residents, particularly youths and women, to support the party and vote for its candidates in the National Assembly, governorship and State House of Assembly elections.

He specifically called on voters to participate in the January 16, 2027 National Assembly elections and the February 6, 2027 governorship and State Assembly elections.

Also speaking, the PDP National Secretary, Senator Samuel Anyanwu, expressed confidence that Odii would win across the state’s 171 electoral wards and 13 local government areas.

Anyanwu attributed the candidate’s popularity to his longstanding interventions and support for individuals and communities across the state.

He urged party members to intensify grassroots mobilisation and ensure that the PDP’s campaign message reached every community ahead of the elections.

The presentation of flags to Odii, Mgbebu and other PDP candidates formally marked the commencement of the party’s campaign in Ebonyi State ahead of the 2027 general elections.

 

The post 2027: Odii vows to end poverty, industrialise Ebonyi appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: EERC urges Nsukka residents to protect electricity infrastructure, shun energy theft
articles.summary:
From Felix Ikem, Nsukka

The Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the Enugu State Electricity Regulatory Commission (EERC), Mr Chijioke Okonkwo, has urged Nsukka residents to protect electricity infrastructure, shun energy theft and pay bills promptly to enable MainPower to improve service delivery.

Okonkwo gave the charge in Nsukka yesterday during a stakeholders’ engagement organised by the commission to sensitise electricity consumers in the area and obtain feedback on the activities of MainPower, their electricity service provider.

He said the engagement was part of the EERC’s mandate to ensure a transparent, accountable and customer-focused electricity market in the state, while bringing electricity regulation closer to the people.

According to him, the initiative provides consumers with an opportunity to interact directly with the regulator and their electricity service provider.

He explained that the engagement was designed to address electricity-related complaints by providing residents with a platform to raise concerns over poor power supply, faulty transformers, estimated billing, metering and other service challenges.

“Today, consumers were educated on their rights to fair billing, proper metering, quality service and access to complaint resolution mechanisms, as well as the importance of protecting electricity installations in their communities to ensure sustainable power supply.

“We equally gave MainPower an opportunity to explain its performance and respond to consumers’ grievances.

“The engagement also provided a platform for resolving disagreements between electricity consumers and service providers through dialogue and regulatory intervention,” he said.

Okonkwo further said the commission was committed to ensuring that Enugu State developed a functional and efficient electricity market that served the interests of all critical stakeholders, particularly consumers.

“We have let the people know that we are here like a referee in a football match. Customers are not limited to the operators they have; they can also have their issues dealt with by the independent regulatory agency,” he said.

The chairman urged customers whose complaints remained unresolved by the distribution company to escalate their cases to the regulator within 30 days for redress.

Speaking, the State Commissioner for Energy and Mineral Resources, Hon. Enyinaya Ogbonna, said the ministry intended to carry out a sensitisation campaign across the 17 local government areas in the state to enable residents to know their rights as electricity users.

“We, as a ministry, are going to provide equilibrium to make sure that the Enugu State electricity market grows. So, what we are doing here today is critical because we are going to communicate the feedback to the governor for prompt action.

“The target of this administration is to make Enugu the destination of every investor, and to achieve that, we intend to ensure that there is affordable and reliable electricity, even in the rural areas of the state,” he said.

The engagement, which featured an educative and interactive session, as well as a question-and-answer segment, attracted participants from various communities in Nsukka Local Government Area, representatives of private institutions in the area, and members of the Enugu Electricity Distribution Company (EEDC).

In a remark, the Managing Director of MainPower Electricity Distribution Limited (MEDL), Enugu State, Dr Ernest Mupwaya, commended the EERC for the stakeholders’ engagement, which made it possible for MainPower to interact with its customers face-to-face.

The MD announced that 10,000 customers in Nsukka LGA would be enumerated and metered soon, as meters for the exercise were already available.

He assured customers that all complaints raised during the engagement would be duly addressed by MainPower, adding that the company would continue to work hard to ensure that customers received quality service.

“The vision of Governor Peter Mbah of Enugu State in establishing MainPower Electricity Company is to ensure that Enugu State residents enjoy the best electricity supply in the country,” he said.

Mupwaya, however, urged customers to ensure prompt payment of their electricity bills, protect electricity infrastructure in their areas, and avoid electricity theft to enable MainPower to serve them better.

Earlier, in a remark, the Nsukka LGA Chairman, Chief Jude Asogwa, represented by Mrs Anthonia Okwor, a staff member of the council, thanked the EERC for the stakeholders’ engagement aimed at sensitising electricity customers in the area and obtaining their feedback on the activities of MainPower, their electricity provider.

The post EERC urges Nsukka residents to protect electricity infrastructure, shun energy theft appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: NDC knocks Abdulsalami peace committee, calls it ‘toothless bulldog’ over attacks on opposition
articles.summary:
From Adesuwa Tsan, Abuja

The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has described the National Peace Committee led by former Head of State, General Abdulsalami Abubakar, as a “toothless bulldog”, accusing it of failing to speak out against alleged attacks on opposition parties despite its mandate to promote peaceful political conduct.

It said the committee had failed to demonstrate even the moral courage to condemn the violence allegedly directed at its members and supporters, claiming that it had recorded at least 17 incidents of attacks.

The National Publicity Secretary of the NDC, Osa Director, who stated this in an interview with Saturday Sun, said neither Abdulsalami nor the committee’s chairman, Bishop Matthew Hassan Kukah, had reached out to the party over the incidents.

Abubakar serves as Chairman, while Bishop Matthew Hassan Kukah is the convenedr of the committee.

He said although the committee lacked constitutional or statutory powers to sanction those who violated the peace agreement, it had a moral obligation to condemn political violence.

“The Bishop Kukah committee is a toothless bulldog. I mean, we know that they don’t have any constitutional or statutory means of bringing violators of the agreement to book.

“But at least on moral grounds, they should speak out against all the violence perpetrated against the Nigeria Democratic Congress. At least as at last count, 17.

“Neither Bishop Kukah nor General Abdulsalami has called us, so it is a big shame, and it is up to them to do what they want to do.

“But I believe there should be a moral compulsion on their part to make statements condemning the spate of violence in the country,” he said.

Director also accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of repeatedly attacking opposition parties, insisting that the NDC had never engaged in violence against any political party.

“We have never engaged in violence with any political party. They are the ones who always attack us. So Nigerians should insist that they play by the rules and international best practices and stop attacking the opposition,” he said.

He called on security agencies, particularly the Nigeria Police Force, to discharge their constitutional responsibilities without political interference, warning against turning the force into an instrument of the ruling party.

“We don’t want an APC police; we want a police that is paid and sustained by Nigerian taxpayers’ money. So if only they’ll do their job,” he said.

The NDC spokesman said the party’s strategy for protecting its members in forthcoming campaigns is to continue notifying security agencies ahead of its campaigns and other political activities, expressing hope that pressure from Nigerians, the media and the international community would help prevent further violence.

 

The post NDC knocks Abdulsalami peace committee, calls it ‘toothless bulldog’ over attacks on opposition appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: Accept Senator Kalu’s adoption as consensus candidate by stakeholders – Cleric to other contestants
articles.summary:
Described as best Senator yet in Abia North

From Okey Sampson, Umuahia

A cleric, Bishop Silas Eke of the Kingly People’s Assembly has commended the people of Abia State, particularly political and community stakeholders in Abia North Senatorial District, for adopting Senator Orji Uzor Kalu as their consensus candidate for the 2027 senatorial election and urged other contestants to accept the adoption.

This is as another cleric, Evangelist Ifeanyi Ogbonna has described Kalu as the best senator Abia North had produced and needs to be re-elected.

Bishop Eke urged candidates of other political parties seeking to represent Abia North in the Senate to accept the adoption of the former governor in good faith.

Eke noted that the development of Abia North should take precedence over individual political ambitions, stressing that unity among stakeholders was essential to attracting greater federal presence and accelerating the socio-economic development of the district.

“I sincerely appreciate the people of Abia State, particularly Abia North, for the unity they have demonstrated. Our collective development must remain paramount. Those aspiring to represent the district should embrace the adoption of Senator Orji Uzor Kalu in good faith and congratulate him,” Eke said.

While congratulating Senate Kalu for his adoption by the stakeholders, he expressed optimism that Kalu’s return to the Senate would yield greater developmental benefits for Abia North and the Igbo nation at large.

Eke also expressed support for the vision concerning Kalu attributed to the Leader of INRI Evangelical Spiritual Church, Primate Elijah Ayodele, maintaining that Abia North stood to benefit from the opportunities envisaged by the prominent cleric.

He emphasised that the ultimate measure of political leadership should be its impact on the lives of ordinary citizens and the opportunities it creates for future generations.

Meanwhile, another cleric, Evangelist Ifeanyi Ogbonna has described Kalu as the best senator Abia North had produced, maintaining that his approach to legislative representation had raised public expectations of federal lawmakers across Abia State.

Speaking during the Kalu Ward to Ward tour of Item in Bende Local Government Area, Ogbonna noted that Kalu’s emergence as a senator had changed the perception of many Abians about the responsibilities of lawmakers, particularly their capacity to facilitate major infrastructural projects.

According to the cleric, Kalu’s interventions in road construction had opened the eyes of Abians to what legislators could achieve, thereby placing other federal lawmakers under pressure to deliver projects to their constituents.

“Since Senator Orji Uzor Kalu was elected to the Senate, other federal lawmakers have come under pressure to perform. He opened the eyes of Abians to the fact that a lawmaker can facilitate the construction of roads and other major infrastructural projects,” Ogbonna said.

The cleric further highlighted Kalu’s investment in human capital development, noting that the senator had facilitated overseas scholarships and training opportunities for more than 60 beneficiaries.

“From road construction to human capital development, his interventions have been remarkable. More than 60 people have benefited from overseas scholarships and training opportunities,” he added.

Addressing the gatherings, Kalu commended the people of Item for their impressive turnout and the orderliness demonstrated throughout the tour.

The former governor acknowledged the outstanding developmental challenges confronting the communities and pledged to facilitate additional road networks, solar-powered streetlights and human capital development programmes if re-elected.

“I appreciate the people of Item for the orderliness maintained throughout our engagements. We acknowledge your needs, and we will continue to do more,” Kalu said.

The senator also canvassed support for the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, urging constituents to vote for the APC “from top to bottom” in the 2027 general elections.

articles.title: Over 70 aviation professionals expected at NCATAA’s Pan-African aviation conference in Lagos

In a bid to address some of the challenges confronting the aviation sector in Nigeria and other African countries, the Nigeria College of Aviation Technology Alumni Association (NCATAA), has concluded plans to host a Pan-African Aviation Conference in Lagos.

Billed to grace the event are policymakers, regulators, airline operators, airport operators, aviation agencies, financiers, training institutions and professionals from Nigeria and across Africa.

Ahead of the event, the President of NCATAA, Ali Magashi, said the conference will move beyond usual rhetoric to practical implementation of decisions reached.

“Nigeria cannot lead African aviation on potential alone. This conference is about moving from talk to measurable action – with timelines, owners and outcomes. We are bringing the people who make decisions into the same room as the people who live with the consequences,” Magashi said.

He also said over 70 leading aviation professionals will take part in seven strategic conversations, an industry exhibition, interactive panels and a leadership roundtable.

Key sessions include, aviation finance and insurance, airports infrastructure MRO and maintenance, SAATM and African connectivity as well as aviation safety, regulation and governance.

Others are, airspace, communication, navigation, surveillance and air traffic management, weather, aviation security, training and human capital development. There would also be executive leadership roundtable on the topic, ‘Where we are today and what must change in Nigerian aviation’.

articles.title: 2027: Osun monarch tasks political leaders, stakeholders on peace, divisive politics
articles.summary:
By Sunday Ani

The Olowu of Kuta, Oba Hammeed Oyelude, has called on political leaders, stakeholders and residents of Osun State to shun bitterness and divisive politics as preparations for the 2027 general elections gather momentum.

The monarch also congratulated three senior officials of the Osun State Government who were recently reappointed by Governor Ademola Adeleke, urging them to justify the confidence reposed in them through greater commitment to service.

The three reappointed officials include the Secretary to the State Government (SSG), Bobagunwa Teslim Igbalaye; Chief of Staff to the Governor, Alhaji Kazeem Akinleye and the Governor’s Spokesperson, Mallam Olawale Rasheed.

In a congratulatory statement from his palace, Oba Oyelude, who holds the title of Tegbosun III, described their reappointment as an opportunity to demonstrate greater dedication to the administration and contribute meaningfully to the development of the state.

He urged the officials to redouble their efforts during the governor’s second tenure, stressing the need for them to justify the renewed confidence placed in them by their principal.

He also extended his goodwill to Gov Adeleke, wishing him a successful and impactful second term in office.

He expressed hope that the administration would sustain its commitment to good governance and the overall development of Osun State.

Concerning the political atmosphere before the 2027 general elections, the Olowu called on politicians and residents to exercise restraint and conduct themselves responsibly in their political engagements.

He warned against political bitterness, hostility and divisive tendencies, stressing that the interest of the state should take precedence over partisan considerations.

According to him, Osun, popularly known as the State of the Living Spring, must remain peaceful and united, despite political differences among its people.

The monarch further urged political actors to embrace tolerance and peaceful coexistence, noting the importance of maintaining harmony as political activities gradually intensify ahead of the next general elections.

He prayed for sustained peace, unity and tranquillity across the state.

articles.title: Loud explosions rock Riyadh as Houthis attack Saudi ports
articles.summary:
Loud explosions rock Riyadh as Houthis attack Saudi ports

Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Wed, 11/25/2026 - 21:13

Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman expected to travel to the US next month for G-20 in first trip since start of war

This aerial photograph shows a view of the Riyadh skyline on 23 November 2026

Off

Fresh explosions rocked Riyadh on Wednesday as Yemen's Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea ports of Jeddah and Jazan, as the kingdom’s deterrence and defensive capabilities continue to be challenged.

The Houthis said that both strikes on the ports “resulted in damage” while the Saudi-led coalition acknowledged that a projectile hit the port of Jazan, resulting in minor damage and no casualties.

The port strikes followed an attack on Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia’s largest refinery. Argus Media, which covers commodity markets, said the Houthis landed two successful blows on the facility, one at the refinery and one at the export terminal. The Houthis say they bombed Ras Tanura as retaliation for the Saudi attack on the port of Hodeidah controlled by the group.

Saudi Arabia is shooting down the majority of Houthi missiles and drones fired at it, Arab and Western officials tell Middle East Eye, but it has failed to protect key assets like energy facilities, financial centres and airports.

Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has tried to rally the US and regional states to his side. Egypt, Pakistan, Turkey and Syria have all sent or committed to delivering military support to Saudi Arabia, but with the exception of Syria - which has sent drone operators - the assistance is defensive.

The Crown Prince met US Central Command chief admiral Brad Cooper, the commander of forces in the Middle East, last week. MEE first reported the planned meeting, which was the third since fighting with the Houthis resumed in July.

The US, Saudi Arabia's top military supplier, however has not publicly committed additional support to the kingdom, although it has troops and advisers inside the country.

Iran tensions simmer

Semafor reported on Wednesday that Mohammed bin Salman will travel to the US next month for the G-20 summit in Miami. Diplomats have speculated for months whether the de facto leader of Saudi Arabia would leave the kingdom amid Houthi strikes and the chances of a new US-Israeli attack on Iran.

'Turn on the weapons spigot': Saudi Arabia asks partners for gear to deter Houthis

Read More »

Tensions between the US and Iran have been simmering for months, with the two sides exchanging blows in the Strait of Hormuz and at some land targets. The US has conducted strikes on Iran’s mainland while Tehran has responded with attacks on US military sites in Kuwait and Bahrain.

Iran said on Wednesday that an oil tanker hit a naval mine and caught fire in a "restricted zone" in the Strait of Hormuz, according to the semi-official Fars news agency.

Brent, the international oil benchmark, was up 2.5 percent on Wednesday, trading at $84 per barrel.

The Trump administration says that it is not interested in resuming the war on Iran for now, and instead wants to use economic means to collapse the government, mainly through a blockade on Iranian ports.

Iran has been hit by debilitating inflation, although regional officials who have traveled to the capital have reported busy restaurants and a sense of calm. Fars said on Wednesday that a substantial shipment of dollar banknotes had entered Iran from a neighbouring country.

articles.title: US ambassador to Israel undercuts Trump's announcement that aid to Israel will end this year
articles.summary:
US ambassador to Israel undercuts Trump's announcement that aid to Israel will end this year

Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Wed, 11/25/2026 - 18:44

The president's abrupt announcement came on the morning of the midterm elections earlier this month

Students carry placards depicting US President Donald Trump and Israel's caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu carrying guns, as they march during a general strike over rising living costs and military spending called by the CGIL trade union, in Milan, Italy, on 20 November 2026 (Claudia Greco/Reuters)

Off

US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee has undercut US President Donald Trump's assertion earlier this month that he "won't be paying Israel" by the end of this year.

Huckabee, the former governor of Arkansas who is an evangelical pastor and a staunch Zionist - by his own description - said on Tuesday at a conference in Tel Aviv that he's "not certain that there will be a cessation on an abrupt basis by the end of this year". 

That's because Washington currently gives Israel $3.8bn a year, in a 10-year memorandum of understanding that runs from 2019 to 2028.

The package also includes $3.3bn in foreign military financing and $500m in cooperative missile defence programmes.

In May, the Israeli defence ministry said that the two sides had begun formal talks to replace the current memorandum, with discussions focusing on joint investment in research, development and weapons production.

The suggested framework was to move the relationship from aid to a more reciprocal partnership. 

The Congressional Research Service, a non-partisan research body that advises the US Congress, further confirmed this in a June report that US and Israeli officials were discussing a possible shift after 2028 away from direct military aid and towards joint programmes.

Israel, a full-scale partner

In July, the Republican-controlled House of Representatives narrowly passed a $1.5 trillion budget for the US Department of War, and the bill included a controversial provision that would permanently integrate US and Israeli military tech advancements in a way that would - as Netanyahu put it - turn Israel from a foreign aid recipient to a full-scale partner. 

Future presidents would not be able to simply withdraw from such a project. 

Kushner says Israel is becoming a 'pariah' as his Board of Peace plans stall

Read More »

The National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) is must-pass legislation, as it is needed to fund all of the Pentagon's operations in the year to come. The Senate will have to consider it soon.

But emboldened by the incoming Democratic majority in January, a dozen Democrats, led by Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen, are seeking to remove the provisions related to Section 219, which establishes the "United States–Israel Defense Technology Cooperation Initiative".

The project would identify jointly developed or Israeli-origin technologies for potential integration into US systems; ensure collaborative research initiatives involving government, private sector and academic institutions in both countries protect "sensitive technology"; and ultimately align military efforts with the Department of War that include the Irregular Warfare Technical Support Directorate, the Defense Innovation Unit, the Missile Defense Agency and the United States Space Command, among others. 

Huckabee said at the Institute for National Security Studies conference on Tuesday that American lives are saved "every day" because "we pick up intelligence from our partners in Israel". 

Military ties continue

On 3 November, Trump said that his administration will not give its yearly military aid to Israel starting next year, because of a prior understanding he made with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. 

Trump added that weapon sales and other forms of military cooperation would continue. 

Speaking on Fox News, the president said that the two had agreed months ago to end the military aid since Israel no longer needed it.

Britain must stand firm against Nusseibeh's UN candidacy

Read More »

“Now, as far as paying Israel, Bibi Netanyahu and I have made a deal that we give Israel $4bn a year, and we made a deal months ago that we're stopping,” Trump said.

“We've already agreed that by the end of this year we won't be paying Israel. Now we'll help Israel if they need it,” he added.

Trump said Israel would be able to purchase weapons from the United States and other countries, suggesting that the change would affect the form of assistance rather than bring an end to military ties.

"They can buy whatever they want. They can buy whatever they want. So can Europe. We make the greatest weapons in the world," he said.

The comments came as Republican lawmakers and establishment Democrats running for Congress - as well as hundreds of statewide races - faced growing electoral pressure over support for Israel ahead of the midterm elections.

And indeed, the so-called blue tsunami, led by an energised progressive Democratic movement that wants to curb US aid to Israel, washed over Capitol Hill and state legislatures, including several governorships.

articles.title: The gold-filled mountains of Chad that hold the key to Libya's crisis and Sudan's war
articles.summary:
The gold-filled mountains of Chad that hold the key to Libya's crisis and Sudan's war

Submitted by
MEE correspondent
on
Wed, 11/25/2026 - 14:23

A mining dispute in a town of a few thousand people tucked away in the remote roof of the Sahara has become entangled with an arms corridor sustaining one of the world’s deadliest wars

The Tibesti mountains run through northern Chad into southern Libya, and are home to the Tubu people (MEE)

Off

Deep inside the Tibesti mountains of northern Chad, in the central Sahara, the town of Miski sits surrounded by a succession of never-ending wadis. 

A couple of families live at the top of each of these valleys and in August, when the rainy season comes, the wadis become a river that washes through the mountains. When the rains go, the valleys become green and camels feed on them.

A remote volcanic range characterised by rugged, bare rock, rivers of lava and volcanoes that climb to 3,000 metres, the Tibesti, which runs through northern Chad across the border into southern Libya, is sometimes called the roof of the Sahara. 

These mountains are home to the Tubu, an indigenous community whose territory also includes a part of southern Libya, northern Niger and northwestern Sudan.

And the valleys that surround the town of Miski contain vast deposits of a precious metal that throughout human history has been prized almost above anything else: gold. 

The mountains, too, are filled with antimony, a toxic heavy metal that is putting the ecosystem of this indigenous community at severe risk and is also exported in great quantities. 

For decades, the gold that sits in this remote place has been one of the drivers of armed conflict between the Tubu and the Libyan, then Chadian states. 

Now, the Tubu find themselves caught up in a web of warfare and illicit trade that stretches out from Chad into Libya, Sudan and over the sea to the United Arab Emirates, from where arms and supplies are flown to proxy armies, militias and paramilitaries. 

On 14 October, armed clashes broke out in Miski.

The day after fighting began, the Chadian army’s general staff accused Miski’s self-defence committee - a local armed group descended from the Tubu institution of village guardianship - of breaking a peace agreement struck between them and the army last year by attacking the National Brigade for the Control of Mining Activities.

The army gave the Tubu group an ultimatum: lay down your arms at once or be treated as rebels. In response, the committee accused the brigade of firing first and of opening new mining fronts in grazing lands, in violation of the Bardai peace accord signed last year.

The gold ends up in Dubai…'yet we do not have a single clinic in Miski or a single paved road in the whole of the Tibesti' 

- Tubu commander

One Tubu commander in Miski told Middle East Eye that last year Chad had exported over $1bn worth of gold and more than 15,000 tonnes of antimony, all sourced from the Tibesti mountains.

Almost all this gold ends up in the UAE, in the gold market of Dubai.

“And yet we do not have a single clinic in Miski or a single paved road in the whole of the Tibesti,” the commander said. “We won’t let this continue.”

Since the armed clashes broke out in October, the Chadian army has moved considerable numbers of troops and armoured vehicles into the Tibesti.  

The situation on the ground, according to one Chadian army officer who spoke to MEE, is difficult for government troops. “We are fighting the mines and the mountains in Miski,” he said.

This fighting has not stopped: scores of people have died in the clashes and the Chadian army has conducted multiple drone strikes across the mountain range.

Weapons corridor

Miski’s uprising appears, on the surface, to be a local fight over gold - and in a large part, it is. 

But it is unfolding inside a region that has become one of the most consequential, least scrutinised arms corridors in Africa: a route that, according to United Nations investigators and extensive reporting from Middle East Eye, has carried weapons, fuel and fighters from the UAE through Libya and Chad to the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in Sudan. 

How the UAE continued supporting Sudan's RSF through Haftar and Libya

Read More »

These weapons are part of a network of arms and mercenaries that spans swathes of north and central Africa, utilised not just in Sudan but by organised criminal groups and armed entities across the Sahel.   

Between October 2024 and the end of 2025, according to a UN Panel of Experts report, heavy cargo aircraft made 458 flights between military airports in the UAE or the Emirati base at Bosaso in the breakaway Somali region of Puntland and eastern Libya.  

Some 239 of these landed at Kufra, a town about 300km from the Sudan border that was transformed, in the months before the RSF took el-Fasher in October 2025, into a fortified logistics hub complete with new hangars and scheduled flights. 

Separately, as reported by MEE and confirmed by UN experts, the UAE was using Amdjarass, in eastern Chad, to land cargo planes.

Senior Egyptian army sources told MEE earlier this year that the Emiratis have a military operations room inside Amdjarass airport to coordinate with the RSF.

Just over 100km from the border with Darfur, the vast western region of Sudan controlled by the RSF, Amdjarass is a Zaghawa-dominated town that is the home region of Chad’s president, Mahamat Idriss Deby, and the site of a lavish state infrastructure programme that residents of Tibesti, 1,300km away and without a single paved road or a functioning hospital between them, have started to openly resent.

Abu Dhabi continues to deny supplying the Rapid Support Forces.

Haftar’s expanding footprint

In November 2025, Chad and the UAE-backed Haftar family’s Libyan Arab Armed Forces (LAAF), de facto commanded by Khalifa Haftar’s son Saddam, formed a joint border force covering roughly 1,050km of shared frontier.

The Haftars are not just in control of eastern Libya: leaked details of US adviser Massad Boulos’s plan to unify Libya propose Saddam Haftar as president of a government that would continue to be led by Prime Minister Abdul Hamid Dbeibah. 

Chad’s government has two reasons to want this partnership, and they reinforce each other. 

One is logistical: Chad and Haftar can cement their relationship in the eastern Libyan corridor that carries Emirati arms to the Rapid Support Forces in Sudan. 

The other is that a joint border force hems in the Tubu, who have supplied the armed resistance to Mahamat Deby’s government and to Haftar’s forces alike. 

Jalel Harchaoui, an analyst focusing on Libya and political economy, told Middle East Eye that when the deal was initially struck, the Tubu were not part of the thinking.

The only connection in the remote area - Starlink (MEE)

“It was to ensure better security along the route between Chad and Libya, especially with the passage via Ma’tan as-Sarra in Libya down through Chad to Amdjarass and then on to Darfur,” he said.

This “security problem” included armed groups attacking the convoys headed to Darfur to supply the RSF, Harchaoui said. There was also the need to build further cooperation between Emirati allies who were not natural bedfellows.

“Saddam Haftar and Mahamat Deby don’t get along, so there was a need to please the UAE by doing a joint force. And the agreement was never that the joint force would be pushed to the west, it was really to cover the northeastern corner of Chad,” Harchaoui said.

That changed earlier this year, when Saddam Haftar “ran into trouble” with armed Tubu groups like the Southern Liberation Operations Room (Slor), which is led by Mohamed Wardougou, a Libyan Tubu, and often hides out in northern Niger.

Haftar asked Chad to move forces to the west, arguing correctly, according to Harchaoui, “that Wardougou’s activism served as a shot in the arm for the anti-Deby Chadian group Front for Change and Concord in Chad (Fact) in northern Niger”.

History of revolt

This move played into the Tubu’s long record of rising up against the central governments of Chad, going back to the country’s independence from France in 1960. 

Their most recent armed revolt, in April 2021, culminated in the death on the front line of President Idriss Deby Itno, who had decided at the age of 68 to command his forces in person. His son Mahamat succeeded him.

In Libya too, the Tubu rose against Muammar Gaddafi, and after his fall in 2011, they held sway over vast stretches of southern Libya until 2021, when Haftar’s forces pushed into the areas they had controlled. The containment effort carries a human cost well beyond Tibesti. 

In Libya, Tubu communities describe a steady tightening around their citizenship, with human rights researchers long having flagged discriminatory practices such as treating the Tubu as second-class citizens and stopping them from obtaining passports and IDs. 

'We do not want to be part of a bigger game… We just want peace and justice and foremost, transparency in mining and the development of our region'

- Tubu defence committee member

On 14 October, the same day gunfire broke out in Miski, Libya’s attorney general in Tripoli said he was prepared to strip the 28,000 families registered at Murzuq, in the Fezzan region of southwest Libya, of their Libyan nationality, citing alleged forgery. 

Because the overwhelming majority of Libya’s Tubu are registered through that one civil registry, the announcement reads as an existential threat: if carried through, most of Libya’s Tubu would become stateless.

On the border between Libya and Niger, Wardougou’s Slor group has fought a running battle with Haftar’s forces, using northern Niger as a rear base. The Slor’s declared aim is to remove Haftar’s men from southern Libya.

In July, photographs circulated online showing Chadian soldiers at Libya’s Wigh airbase, near the Nigerien border - evidence, the group’s leadership says, that Chad is fighting on Haftar’s behalf. 

On 20 October, the LAAF arrested a former Chadian minister and senior opposition figure, Hassan Soukaya, as he tried to cross from Libya into Niger, and handed him to the Chadian army.

Days later, Niger’s government publicly accused the Chadian military, with alleged French support, of carrying out a drone strike on 24 October near the Salvador Pass that killed two civilians. The attack was reportedly meant to target Slor positions in Libya, but hit Nigerien territory by accident.

The UAE-Israel desert axis

On 19 October, Israel’s second-ever ambassador to Chad landed in N’Djamena to present her credentials to Deby.

Since taking power after his father’s death in 2021, Deby has made a point of binding Chad ever closer to the UAE and Israel: diplomatic relations with Israel were restored in 2022, and the first Israeli ambassador in more than half a century - since Chad broke off ties in 1972 - was received shortly afterwards. Despite this, in November 2023, Chad recalled its ambassador from Israel, citing “the unprecedented tide of deadly violence” inside Gaza.  

Chadian alignment with the UAE is not only military. As previously reported by MEE, the Emiratis offered Deby “more than a billion dollars” to “flip Chad towards supporting the RSF” after the war in Sudan began, according to former CIA analyst Cameron Hudson.

Senior UAE and regional officials referred to ICC over role in Sudan atrocities

Read More »

That figure now looks like loose change. In May 2025, in Abu Dhabi, Chad unveiled Chad Connexion 2030, a $30bn national development strategy to remake the infrastructure of a landlocked country from the ground up.

The UAE was, by a wide margin, its most important bilateral underwriter, securing $20.5bn in total backing and signing 18 contracts of its own worth over $6.2bn. 

Among the headline projects: an 800-km Etihad rail line to Cameroon’s port of Douala, a 50 MWp solar plant by Global South Utilities, industrial zones, Abu Dhabi Ports logistics hubs, and critical-mineral exploration permits. 

The partnership has tightened Chad’s dependence on the UAE and has become, in effect, the economic lifeline of Deby’s administration. To the west, Chad is already at odds with its neighbour Niger, which has drawn closer to Algeria.

In late October, Algeria deployed troops to Niger, the first time it had done this outside its borders since 1973. The move came days after Niger’s military government survived a coup attempt on 28 August.

Algeria’s move into Niger, according to the retired Algerian diplomat Amar Belani, is designed to counter what he described as “a destabilisation strategy actively involving the United Arab Emirates, Morocco, Israel and certain French proxies.”

The current geopolitical shifts, Belani went on, together with all they entail by way of rivalry and intervention by foreign actors, mean that “new tools, such as a show of presence including at the military level, are no longer a taboo and will be utilised to draw and reinforce Algeria’s red lines.”

Borderlands unrest

What is forming, in other words, is not one war but two rival blocs assembling around unrest in the desert borderlands. 

Rape, ransom and execution: The road out of Sudan's el-Fasher

Read More »

On one side: the Sudanese Armed Forces (which receives backing from Egypt and Turkey), Niger, Algeria, and the Tubu in Libya and Chad. On the other: the RSF, the Haftars, the UAE, Ethiopia and the Chadian state, with the French leaning towards this camp.

And the local fights and the larger one are no longer separate. A mining dispute in a town of a few thousand people tucked away deep in the remote mountains of Chad has become entangled with an arms corridor sustaining one of the world’s deadliest wars, with a succession contest inside Libya’s eastern military establishment, and a Sahelian realignment redrawing alliances from Algiers to Khartoum. 

“We do not want to be part of a bigger game,” one member of the Tubu defence committee in Miski told MEE. “We just want peace and justice and foremost, transparency in mining and the development of our region.”

But whether it remains a local counter-insurgency or becomes the spark for something larger will depend less on what happens in the mountains of Tibesti than on decisions being made in Abu Dhabi, Benghazi and Paris.

Sahel

Oscar Rickett

Miski, Chad

articles.title: Houthis say they attacked Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery in retaliation for deadly strikes
articles.summary:
Houthis say they attacked Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery in retaliation for deadly strikes

Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Wed, 11/25/2026 - 15:56

Yemeni movement says the refinery attack was in retaliation to Saudi strikes, including one that killed at least 26 people earlier this week

This satellite image shows a large smoke cloud billowing over Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery on 25 November 2026 (Planet Labs PBC/Handout via Reuters)

Off

Yemen's Houthi movement claimed responsibility for an attack on Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery, Ras Tanura, on Wednesday, describing it as retaliation for repeated Saudi strikes that have killed scores of civilians.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said in a post on X that the refinery attack caused fires and came in retaliation for the "brutal Saudi aggression against our country, including its targeting of passenger buses and citizens' trucks in the Al-Maqatirah district of Lahij, as well as other crimes in the capital, Sanaa, and the governorates."

The attack in the district of Lahij earlier this week killed at least 26 people.

In a follow-up post on X, Saree responded to Saudi threats to retaliate against Yemen's civilian Hodeidah port, which Saudi Arabia has already bombed, by warning that all "enemy Saudi ports along the Red Sea coast will be targets".

"We warn employees, workers and those near these ports to evacuate them immediately and stay away, and we call on all shipping companies to remove their ships from those ports immediately," the post added.

Ansar Allah, known as the Houthis, which controls the capital Sanaa and much of north and western Yemen, has been firing missiles at Saudi airports, oil infrastructure and office buildings since Yemen's frozen civil war reignited in July in a spillover from the Israeli-US war on Iran.

Riyadh broke the ceasefire, which also included Saudi Arabia, when it bombed Sanaa's international airport on 13 July.

Since then, the Saudi military has struggled to contain the Houthis and their ability to counter Saudi-backed forces in Yemen.

The ongoing attacks are wreaking havoc on the Saudi economy, oil infrastructure and the country's international image.

Airlines have cancelled international flights from the Saudi capital, Riyadh, while previous attacks on the country’s oil infrastructure have disrupted oil supplies.

The attacks have also forced Saudi Arabia to postpone or cancel major international events, including football's AFC Asian Cup and the flagship Future Investment Initiative conference.

Earlier on Wednesday, the Saudis said that air defences had intercepted and destroyed four drones in Ras Tanura in the country's Eastern Province. They did not deny that the attack had struck the oil refinery there.

Who are Yemen's Houthis and what do they want?

Read More »

Satellite images reviewed by Reuters showed large swathes of thick black smoke around the refinery, covering an area spanning around 600 square kilometres.

The Houthis have previously targeted Ras Tanura, which has a refining capacity of 550,000 barrels per day, during the conflict.

The refinery forms part of a strategic complex on the kingdom's Gulf coast facing Iran, through which the country exported most of its oil before the Israel-US war on Iran started on 28 February.

Since then, Saudi Arabia has had to send some of its oil through Yanbu on the west coast along the Red Sea, which receives oil via the East-West pipeline and has also faced attacks.

Separately, Houthi spokesman Saree had also said the group had attacked Riyadh's financial district in three phases.

Saudi civil defence said a strike on Tuesday wounded 11 people at a tower in Riyadh’s financial district. The tallest building in the capital, the tower houses the headquarters of the Public Investment Fund, the kingdom’s sovereign wealth fund. It was the second strike on the tower in less than a week.

The first, on 19 November, damaged the building but caused no injuries. Saudi civil defence posted an image on Tuesday of the landmark tower showing some damage about halfway up the facade, similar to the impact of last week's attack.

articles.title: Jeremy Corbyn and Rashida Tlaib join politicians and legal groups condemning Ulm 5 prosecution
articles.summary:
Jeremy Corbyn and Rashida Tlaib join politicians and legal groups condemning Ulm 5 prosecution

Submitted by
Katherine Hearst
on
Wed, 11/25/2026 - 13:02

Two letters signed by 26 politicians and 31 legal groups demand the 'immediate release' of defendants in Germany

The 'Ulm Five' from left to right: Daniel Tatlow-Devally, Zo Hailu, Crow Tricks, Vi Kovarbasic and Leandra Rollo (supplied)

Off

Jeremy Corbyn and Rashida Tlaib are among dozens of politicians and legal organisations raising alarm over the prosecution and treatment of pro-Palestine activists in Germany.

Two letters issued on Wednesday, signed by 26 politicians and 31 legal groups from across the globe, condemned the treatment of five activists who have been held in pretrial detention for over 14 months.

Daniel Tatlow-Devally, Zo Hailu, Crow Tricks, Vi Kovarbasic and Leandra Rollo, who are from Germany, Spain, Ireland and the UK, were arrested on 8 September following an alleged break-in at the premises of Israeli arms firm Elbit Systems in the southwestern German city of Ulm.

Known as the “Ulm Five”, the group is accused of damaging the building's glass facade and smashing office equipment, including computers, screens and telephones.

In addition to charges of trespass and damage to property, the five are accused of "membership of a criminal organisation", namely Palestine Action Germany, under Section 129 of the German penal code.

The legislation is typically used to target organised crime networks and carries a potential sentence of up to five years in prison.

All the defendants have been held in prolonged pretrial detention, where they report facing restrictive conditions.

Under Section 129, suspects can be held for up to six months before trial, though lawyers say this period has now been significantly extended.

In their letter, the elected officials - including members of the German Bundestag, the European Parliament, the US Congress, the Irish Parliament and other legislatures across Europe and the Americas - called for the activists’ “immediate release”.

They further warned that the implications of their prosecution and treatment extend beyond the five defendants, forming “part of an international effort to discipline opposition to war and to place the interests of arms manufacturers above the rights of peoples and the obligations of international law”.

'Politically inconvenient facts'

Meanwhile, a separate letter signed by 33 legal groups - including the Center for Constitutional Rights, the Punjab Bar Council, European Democratic Lawyers, the American Association of Jurists, the Irish Council for Civil Liberties, the German Association of Democratic Lawyers - warned that the conduct of the trial could constitute a breach of German and international law.

In particular, the letter raises concerns about the courtroom’s security arrangements, which it said obstruct confidential communication between the defendants and their lawyers and could undermine the presumption of justice.

MEE previously reported that the trial, which began on 27 April, is taking place at a high security courtroom in the notorious Stammheim complex.

The defence team has repeatedly protested their clients’ treatment during proceedings, where the defendants are handcuffed and seated behind a glass barrier, preventing confidential communication with their lawyers.

The legal groups also challenged the court’s rejection of multiple applications by defence lawyers to hear expert witnesses. 

MEE previously reported that the court refused to hear weapons expert Dr Shir Hever and international law expert Isabel Feichtner, who were presented by the defence team to give evidence regarding Elbit Systems’ role in Israel’s genocide in Gaza and Germany’s obligations under international law.

The organisations further rejected the use of Section 129 against the defendants, insisting that “the prosecution of specific acts of property damage must not be conflated with the criminalisation of a political protest movement”.

"A criminal trial must establish the relevant facts impartially," they urged. "It must not exclude politically inconvenient facts merely because they concern the conduct of a powerful arms manufacturer or the actions of a state in an ongoing armed conflict".

UNHCR's 2026 appeal targeted $8.5 billion -- of which only $2.9 billion has been raised to date.

Ukrainian foreign minister warns Europe against delaying aid for Ukraine
articles.summary:
Minister of Foreign Affairs Andrii Sybiha has warned that delaying decisions on support for Ukraine could, in the long run, result in significantly higher expenditure for European states on defending their own territory.

Source: Ukrinform, citing Sybiha at a joint press conference in Kyiv with Secretary General of the Council of Europe Alain Berset, as reported by European Pravda

Details: Sybiha noted that the Ukrainian front line is also the line of defence for European security, and that supporting Ukraine is a decision about European self-preservation.

Quote: "If we do not want this war to come to European homes as well, it is important to maintain unity, and it is important to respond resolutely with united, collective decisions to all of Russia's attempts to divide Europe from the US, and to divide... European Union members among themselves. And here we must proceed from the premise that delaying certain decisions could later turn into... significantly greater expenditure to defend one's own specific country."

Details: According to Sybiha, Ukraine counts on its partners taking into account the arguments regarding the necessity of its macro-financial support.

Quote: "The cost of war is rising. Such are the realities now. The enemy – Russia – has increased its war budget, and we must counter proportionately and adequately. It is very important to achieve parity."

Background:

The European Commission proposed providing Ukraine with an additional €45 billion loan, comprising €25 billion in military assistance and €20 billion in budget support.

On 16 October, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told EU leaders at a summit in Brussels that Ukraine would need at least €70 billion in additional financial assistance from its international partners in 2027. Following the summit, the European Council instructed the European Commission to prepare proposals to meet these needs.

On 9 November, European Commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis told European Pravda that the European Commission was exploring the possibility of providing Ukraine with an additional €45 billion in 2027 through a loan mechanism similar to the already agreed €90 billion Ukraine Support Loan.

articles.title: Romania calls on NATO to help repel Russian hybrid attacks
articles.summary:
Romania has called on NATO to take joint measures against hybrid attacks in response to threats from Russia.

Source: dpa, citing a statement by Romanian Foreign Minister Dan Neculăescu, as reported by European Pravda

Details: Hybrid attacks can take the form of military, economic, intelligence and propaganda operations. Hostile states often conceal their involvement. These can also include cyberattacks and disinformation campaigns aimed at influencing public opinion.

Neculăescu noted that until now, this has been an internal matter for individual EU and NATO member states.

Quote: "We need at least a shared situational picture and must systematically look for connections. Are the same actors behind attacks in Germany, Estonia or Romania?"

Details: Neculăescu added that some allies support an approach whereby defence against such threats would become an operational task for NATO. Others reject it, as they see a risk of escalating conflict with Russia.

The Romanian minister accused Russia of seeking to establish exclusive control over the Black Sea.

Quote: "No one else is supposed to be there. Yet we are there: Romania, Bulgaria, Turkey, Ukraine and other countries. We have the right to defend ourselves, but also a right to peace."

Details: Neculăescu remarked that the Black Sea is becoming a weak spot in European security.

Quote: "Nowhere else in Europe do we experience so many incidents that we attribute to Russia: drone attacks, sea mines, attacks on merchant ships."

Details: Recently, merchant ships off the coast of Romania have come under attack several times, allegedly by Russian drones. In some cases, people were killed or injured as a result of these attacks, and vessels sank. In response, NATO has stepped up air and maritime patrols.

Background:

Romanian President Nicușor Dan recently said that NATO's involvement in bringing down Russian missiles and drones over Ukraine would mean joining military hostilities.

Poland previously appealed to its allies to consider the possibility of bringing down Russian missiles over Ukraine when they are heading towards NATO territory.

The request emerged after three Russian missiles violated Polish airspace during a large-scale Russian attack on Ukraine on 20 November.

articles.title: German Rheinmetall may scrap launch of ammunition plant in Ukraine
articles.summary:
German defence conglomerate Rheinmetall is considering shelving its project to build an artillery ammunition manufacturing plant on Ukrainian territory.

Source: German Aid To Ukraine (GAU), citing remarks by Rheinmetall CEO Armin Papperger during a Capital Markets Day presentation in Hamburg

Details: Although nothing has been definitively decided, Papperger believes that Rheinmetall will not proceed with the construction project. One of the reasons cited is the lack of significant progress in establishing production capacities in Ukraine over the past year. Papperger had also previously mentioned "bureaucratic hurdles".

Quote from the GAU: "Papperger explained that the reason for this was that the Ukrainian partners were unwilling to budge from their stance of wanting to produce everything themselves. As things stand, Ukraine already produces a great deal itself, particularly in the area of short- and medium-range artillery ammunition, and the impact of Ukraine on Rheinmetall's business is already very limited."

Details: According to Papperger, Ukraine's defence forces use between 1 million and 1.3 million artillery rounds per year, more than half of which are produced domestically by Ukrainian manufacturers.

Rheinmetall continues to supply Ukraine with artillery ammunition, notably as part of military aid packages from Germany, Denmark, and the Netherlands.

Quote from the GAU: "The CEO sees potential only in the supply of key components, such as presses, to help build up Ukrainian production capacity, and in the supply of very long-range artillery ammunition, for the production of which the Ukrainian industry still lacks the necessary technology."

Background:

Rheinmetall first announced its intention to open an artillery ammunition plant in Ukraine in February 2024. Initially, the company stated plans to manufacture around 150,000 shells per year, while in August 2025 Papperger cited a volume of 300,000 rounds annually. Production was scheduled to launch in 2026.

In September 2025, Ukraine's then-minister of defence Denys Shmyhal said that a site had been allocated for the construction of the plant in one of the safe regions of Ukraine.

By November 2025, Papperger reported that the launch of Rheinmetall's ammunition plant in Ukraine had been postponed to a later date due to a change in its location.

articles.title: Russians attack civilian business in Zhytomyr Oblast: one killed, 12 injured
articles.summary:
One person was killed and 12 more injured in a Russian strike on the Malyn hromada in Zhytomyr Oblast on the afternoon of 27 November. [A hromada is an administrative unit designating a village, several villages, or a town, and their adjacent territories]

Source: Vitalii Bunechko, Head of Zhytomyr Oblast Military Administration; National Police of Ukraine

Quote from Bunechko: "Today, the Malyn hromada came under attack once again. Russian troops attacked a civilian business. Unfortunately, one person was killed and two more were injured."

Details: All relevant services are working at the scene of the strike.

Update: National Police later reported that 12 people, aged from 23 to 61, were injured in the attack.

Background:

On 27 November, Russian forces attacked energy and logistics infrastructure facilities, as well as private residential buildings, in the Zhytomyr and Korosten districts of Zhytomyr Oblast.

On the morning of 25 November, Russian troops attacked the Malyn hromada in Zhytomyr Oblast, killing one person and injuring nine others.

articles.title: Germany adopts 2027 budget with record borrowing, including €12bn in aid for Ukraine
articles.summary:
In Germany, the Bundestag (German parliament) has approved the 2027 budget, which provides for record borrowing of €210 billion as well as financial assistance for Ukraine.

Source: European Pravda, citing Der Spiegel

Details: New borrowing totalling about €210 billion is planned across the core budget and special funds. Last year, budget borrowing stood at €180 billion.

Defence is a key priority, with spending set to rise to nearly €140 billion – a record high since the end of the Cold War. Ukraine will receive €12 billion in aid.

More than a third of the funds will be allocated to the labour and social affairs budget, from which the government will, for instance, subsidise pensions.

Members of parliament voted 317 to 260 in favour of the budget proposed by the grand coalition, which provides for expenditure of €556 billion – roughly €31 billion more than the current year's budget.

Background:

On 9 November, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz tied Berlin's approval of the 2028-2034 EU budget to a commitment from all member states to provide financial support to Ukraine.

Merz also insisted that all EU member states must contribute to funding support for Ukraine and that he does not accept individual states shirking this responsibility.

articles.title: Poland warns of anti-Ukrainian fake news regarding Ukrainian man who set himself on fire in Warsaw
articles.summary:
Senior Inspector Jakub Pacyniak, spokesperson for the Warsaw I District Police Headquarters, reported on 27 November that many false claims and assumptions have appeared on the internet regarding the self-immolation of a Ukrainian citizen outside the Presidential Palace.

Source: Jakub Pacyniak's statement cited by Polish media outlet RMF FM, as reported by European Pravda

Details: In particular, as noted, information regarding the 22-year-old man's Ukrainian citizenship was quickly exploited by some users on X (Twitter) and Facebook to incite anti-Ukrainian sentiment.

The posting and artificial promotion of this type of content is aimed to provoke extreme emotions and polarise public opinion.

Social media users circulated, among other things, fabricated texts, including alleged farewell letters from the man, which purportedly contained threats against the Polish authorities and citizens.

Conspiracy theories have also begun spreading in social media comments, insinuating that the incident was a terrorist act, sabotage, or a political provocation.

Quote from Pacyniak: "At present, we are not releasing information regarding the victim's possible motives. We are aware that various false reports are appearing online, spread either deliberately or unknowingly. As the police, we urge people to obtain information exclusively from reliable sources."

Details: Pacyniak explained that on Wednesday, following the completion of rescue operations, police cordoned off the scene to prevent unauthorised access. An inspection of the site was conducted. An investigative and search team, a forensic specialist, and even a dog handler with a service dog were dispatched there. This was aimed at preserving all evidence so that investigators could reconstruct the sequence of events and establish the motives that drove the young man.

On 26 November, police handed the case materials over to the District Prosecutor's Office in Warsaw, though law enforcement officers have not ceased investigative actions.

Quote from Pacyniak: "In connection with this case, we have already questioned several individuals and documented evidentiary materials. We also have findings regarding the man's place of residence."

Background:

On the evening of 25 November, a man set himself on fire on the square between the Presidential Palace and the Ministry of Culture and National Heritage building in Warsaw.

The Ukrainian Embassy in Poland reported that the self-immolation was committed by a 22-year-old Ukrainian citizen. He was in a critical condition.

Media outlets also reported that the man demanded that Ukrainians in Poland be treated the same as Poles.

articles.title: Russians attack business in Nizhyn: number injured rises to 3 – photos
articles.summary:
Russian forces attacked a business in the city of Nizhyn in Chernihiv Oblast on Friday 27 November, killing three people.

Source: Oleksandr Kodola, Mayor of Nizhyn; National Police in Chernihiv Oblast

Quote from Kodola: "Two people – a man and a woman – were killed today in an enemy attack on a business in the city."

Details: Kodola said four other people were injured and are currently in hospital receiving the necessary medical treatment.

Photo: National Police in Chernihiv Oblast

Early reports indicate that several people may be trapped under the rubble. Emergency services are working at the scene.

Photo: National Police in Chernihiv Oblast

The mayor urged residents to remain calm, refrain from spreading unverified information and trust only official reports.Update: According to the National Police in Chernihiv Oblast, the number of people injured in the Russian strike on a business in Nizhyn has risen to three.

It is reported that an investigation team of the Nizhyn District Department is working at the scene. The police are recording the consequences of this attack on civilians, taking down information about damage and collecting evidence.

The results of the investigation will be recorded in the Unified Register of Pre-Trial Investigations according to Article 438 of the Criminal Code of Ukraine (violation of rules of warfare).

articles.title: Ukraine brings back 11 people from occupation and Russia, including children and deported Oleshky care home resident – photos
articles.summary:
Another group of Ukrainians has been brought back from the temporarily occupied territories (TOT) of Ukraine and Russia. Among them are nine children and two women.

Source: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy; Dmytro Lubinets, Ukrainian Parliament Commissioner for Human Rights

Quote from Zelenskyy: "Nine children, a grandmother accompanying her grandson, and Anastasiia – a resident of the Oleshky Children's Residential Care Institution who needs special support. These children are from the temporarily occupied territories of the Kherson and Zaporizhzhia regions and Crimea.

Valeriia, Marta, Mykola, Ruslan, Sofiia, Davyd, Oleksii, Oleksandr, and the youngest, Artem, who is only eight years old. All of them will receive the assistance they need."

Details: Among those rescued is a 16-year-old boy who, following his mother's death, lived with his grandmother in the TOT. She subjected him to physical and psychological abuse.

Quote from Lubinets: "For a long time, the boy had been trying to leave for the territory controlled by Ukraine to join his sister. However, this proved impossible due to pressure from his grandmother and representatives of the occupation authorities' child protection services. He was repeatedly told that no one was waiting for him at home. Now, the brother and sister will finally be reunited."

Photo: Volodymyr Zelenskyy

Details: A 13-year-old boy and his 17-year-old half-sister were also returned to Ukraine. Following the death of their mother in April 2026, the children were placed under the temporary guardianship of a stranger.

Quote from Lubinets: "They wanted to stay together and continue living with their older maternal half-sister. Now, the children's wish has finally come true."

Photo: Volodymyr Zelenskyy

Details: Other children were forcibly separated from their families. Two biological brothers, aged 17 and 16, lived with their mother in the TOT. After the start of the full-scale invasion, the family planned to leave the occupied area. However, after the father appealed to the occupation commandant's office, the mother was subjected to psychological pressure and threats.

Quote from Lubinets: "The woman was forced to leave, but the children were not allowed to go with her. Throughout this time, the brothers remained in contact with their mother and wanted to return to her. One of the boys has serious health problems: he can barely walk and urgently needs medical examination and treatment. Now they will finally be reunited with their mother."

Details: Another rescuee is an eight-year-old boy who had not seen his mother since 2022. His mother had travelled to Chernihiv Oblast to resolve legal matters, leaving the child with his grandmother in the TOT.

Photo: Volodymyr Zelenskyy

Due to the outbreak of the full-scale war, the woman was unable to return to her son. Now, the grandmother has accompanied the boy to government-controlled Ukrainian territory, where he has been reunited with his mother.

Mariia Lebedieva, field operations project manager at the humanitarian organisation Emile Foundation also reported that Anastasiia Mamotiuk, a resident of an Oleshky care home, was brought back to government-controlled Ukrainian territory.

Background:

The Russians occupied the Oleshky care home in Kherson Oblast in the very first days of the full-scale invasion and began deporting its residents in 2022.

In November 2023, Anastasiia was among three adults taken to Penza, Russia. The young woman reached out for assistance to leave herself, something she had been seeking since 2022, according to Bring Kids Back UA.

In September, Ukrainska Pravda.Zhyttia (Life) wrote that relatives and acquaintances had lost contact with Anastasiia. This occurred at the very moment when the issue of her return to Ukraine was being resolved.

The group of Ukrainians was successfully brought back thanks to the assistance of the First Lady of the United States of America, Melania Trump.

Lubinets noted that "the total number of children who have returned to the territory controlled by Ukraine with Melania Trump's assistance has now reached 40".

In September 2025, another group of children and two young adults aged between 3 months and 18 years were returned to Ukraine from the temporarily occupied territories and Russia.

articles.title: Ukraine strike plant critical to Russia's Iskander missile programme
articles.summary:
Deep-strike units of Ukraine's Special Operations Forces (SOF) struck the Yefremov Synthetic Rubber Plant in Russia's Tula Oblast on the night of 26-27 November.

Source: press service for Special Operations Forces

Details: The Special Operations Forces reported that several SOF drones reached their targets.

The special operation was carried out in coordination with the insurgent movement operating on Russian territory, Chornaya Iskra (Black Spark).

For reference: The Yefremov plant is one of the largest manufacturers of synthetic rubbers in Russia and the country's sole producer of high-molecular-weight polyisobutylene. The plant produces components for solid rocket propellant and plastic explosives.

Its products are used, in particular, in propellant for Iskander ballistic missiles, which the Russians use to strike Ukrainian cities.

articles.title: Italy denies that Zelenskyy coordinated attack on Russian ship in Libya with partners
articles.summary:
Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani has said that Ukraine did not coordinate its actions in Libya with its partners or inform them about its attack on a Russian ship.

Source: Italian TV channel Sky TG24, as reported by European Pravda

Details: Tajani commented on President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's statement that Ukraine had coordinated its actions in Libya with international partners.

"There was never any coordination. The foreign minister said that they would talk to their allies in the future. None of us was informed; no one knew anything about what the Ukrainians were doing in Libya. So what Zelenskyy said is not true," Tajani said.

The president said Ukrainian diplomats work with their counterparts from other countries when Ukraine operates in certain waters, including international waters, or near another country's infrastructure. He stressed that Ukrainian forces "never attack" without coordinating with the country's partners.

Background:

On 23 November, Zelenskyy confirmed that Ukrainian naval drones had sunk the Russian corvette Merkury, which had a Ka-27 helicopter on board, and also struck the dry cargo ship MV Angara, which Russia was using to transport weapons, near the Libyan port of Benghazi.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni later commented on the Ukrainian strikes on Russian ships in the Libyan port of Benghazi, warning against the spread of the war to the Mediterranean Sea.

articles.title: Zelenskyy wants strikes to further disrupt Russian military production

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wants long-range strikes to cause a more significant slowdown in Russian military production.

We made some adjustments to the operational plan – we must achieve a more significant slowdown in Russian military production and certain economic processes."

Background: Earlier on Friday, Zelenskyy summed up the successful strikes carried out by Ukraine's defence forces over the past week against Russian oil facilities and businesses involved in Russia's military-industrial complex.
